programmes.description:
The Bachelor of Arts in International Business (IB-E) at Heilbronn University of Applied Sciences is a dynamic, English-taught programme designed to provide students with a solid foundation in business administration, intercultural competence, and language skills essential for a global career. The curriculum combines core business disciplines with hands-on experience and offers in-depth exposure to international management practices. Students can choose from four majors, allowing them to specialise in areas such as International Management, Marketing, Human Resource Management, or Finance.
For international students, there is an opportunity to master the German language and gain valuable insights into Germany’s dynamic business landscape. German-speaking students, on the other hand, can expand their skill set by learning a third language, such as Arabic, French, Russian, or Spanish, and explore related cultural areas, adding versatility to their professional profiles.
Students enjoy the opportunity to study at one of 90 renowned partner universities worldwide and complete their internship abroad. Based at the modern Heilbronn city campus (named "Bildungscampus"), students benefit from cutting-edge facilities, strong connections with industry professionals, and networking opportunities with leading companies, ensuring a comprehensive education that prepares them for success in the global marketplace.

programmes.description:
This International Business programme is designed for students aiming for international careers.
Join us to explore how global players operate and make decisions, understand the impact of digitalisation, and enhance your multicultural awareness and leadership skills. You can choose to specialise in International Marketing, International Accounting and Reporting, or International Logistics.
All lectures and seminars are held in small groups of approximately 40 students, putting you at the centre of the learning experience.
Our modern curriculum is designed to meet the highest academic standards while emphasising hands-on experience.
Here are some of the key highlights of the programme:
• core business and management courses with a global perspective,
• specialisation courses, including projects with companies and institutions,
• projects tackling global challenges like sustainability, entrepreneurship, and digitalisation,
• an integrated study abroad semester, and
• opportunities for double degree programmes for high-achieving students with business schools in Europe and the U.S.
Our graduates consistently rate the programme highly and typically have no difficulty securing demanding and intellectually stimulating international positions, whether in the finance sector or with industrial companies in Germany and neighbouring countries.
Thanks to Saarbrücken’s location at the heart of Western Europe, students enjoy great flexibility when completing their mandatory internship – for example, in major financial hubs such as Frankfurt or Paris.
Academically, we offer excellent teaching. Two of our professors have received nationwide awards for outstanding teaching in economics. In addition, many of our faculty members bring valuable real-world experience from leading international companies (e.g. Commerzbank or SAP) and top-level public institutions such as the Deutsche Bundesbank.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The first three semesters focus on core economics and business courses (such as Microeconomics, Macroeconomics, Financial Analysis, and Cost Accounting) as well as management courses (such as Operations Management and Strategic Management).
Additionally, you'll explore the technological and legal landscape of global businesses with courses in IT, data science and digitalisation, as well as international contract law. You'll also enhance your academic language skills in English through courses in academic communication & presentation and academic reading & writing.
In your fourth semester, you'll choose your specialisation (International Marketing, International Accounting & Reporting, or International Logistics) and develop your intercultural skills in preparation for studying abroad.
Your fifth semester kicks off with a study abroad experience at one of our partner universities (high-achieving students with a high GPA can apply for a double degree). In your final semester, you'll select three elective courses of your choice and complete your Bachelor's thesis.
For detailed course descriptions, visit our module database: International Business. You can also download our programme flyer here:

programmes.description:
The International Business programme at TH Nürnberg is a seven-semester course, awarding 210 ECTS credits. English is the exclusive language of instruction for the first three semesters and predominant thereafter, with elective courses available in English or German. The programme admits 70 to 80 students annually, with approximately one-third being international, representing around 40 nationalities. This diversity, coupled with the small cohort size, cultivates a global perspective and fosters close, personal connections between students, faculty, and staff.
Graduates acquire a comprehensive understanding of managing in a globalised world, enriched by a mandatory year abroad that includes an internship and a semester at a partner university, seamlessly integrated into the curriculum. Students can specialise in areas such as Finance, Logistics, or Human Resources, tailoring their education to their career goals.
Additionally, the programme offers the opportunity to earn a second full Bachelor’s degree through double-degree partnerships with:
• International College of Management, Sydney, Australia
• Providence University, Taichung, Taiwan
• Seinäjoki University of Applied Sciences, Finland
• Shenzhen Technology University, China
• Tecnológico de Monterrey, Mexico
• Universidad de Granada, Spain
• Universidad de Valparaíso, Chile
This combination of global exposure, specialised knowledge, and dual-degree options equips graduates with the skills and credentials to excel in international business environments.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
Programme Structure and Course Organisation
The International Business programme is a seven-semester degree combining lectures, seminars, language training, and practice-oriented formats. The curriculum builds business fundamentals, integrates compulsory international experience and foreign language skills, and concludes with advanced studies and specialisation. The language of instruction is English.
Semesters 1 to 3: Foundations of Business Studies
During the first three semesters, students attend core modules such as Business Mathematics, Accounting, Marketing, Finance, Economics and Human Resource Management. Teaching formats include lectures supported by seminars and tutorials focusing on exercises, case studies and teamwork. In addition, students complete compulsory language courses (English plus Spanish or French/ German for international students) and soft-skills seminars, e.g. Intercultural Communication.
Semester 4: Internship Abroad
The fourth semester consists of a mandatory 20-week internship abroad. Students gain practical professional experience and apply their academic knowledge in an international working environment.
Semester 5: Study Semester Abroad
In the fifth semester, students study at one of our partner universities outside Germany. Courses are selected from the host institution’s business curriculum and credited towards the IB degree.
Semesters 6 to 7: Advanced Studies and Specialisation
The final two semesters focus on advanced business modules such as International Management with Cases and International Financial Management. Instruction is mainly seminar-based and case-oriented. Elective courses allow students to specialise in areas including Digital Business, Finance, Marketing, HR Management, Logistics, Sustainability, or International Economics. A compulsory Project Work course strengthens practical and analytical skills through an independent project. The programme concludes with a five-month Bachelor’s thesis, which may also be completed in cooperation with a company in Germany or abroad.
Double Degree Options and Career Preparation
Graduates complete the IB programme with solid expertise in global management, strengthened by a year abroad integrated into the curriculum. Combined with specialised knowledge, two foreign languages and international practical experience, graduates are well prepared for careers in internationally active organisations and global business environments. programmes.description:
Study Your Way & Build Your Career in Germany!
Are you aiming for a career in Germany or within German companies operating worldwide? Do you want to understand global markets, work in multicultural teams, and build practical experience during your studies? Then the International Business programme at OTH Amberg-Weiden is the right choice for you.
The programme provides you with a strong foundation in business administration, including subjects such as economics, business mathematics, and statistics. At the same time, you develop key skills for international careers: you strengthen your English proficiency, acquire German language skills, and build intercultural competence in a diverse, international study environment.
A central focus of the programme is practical relevance and employability. Through hands-on projects with companies and close cooperation with regional industry partners, you gain real-world insights into internationally operating businesses. A mandatory internship semester in Germany as well as German language courses as an integral part of the study programme up to an advanced level further prepare you for entering the German labour market.
The curriculum is designed to offer flexibility and individualisation. Especially in the early semesters, hybrid courses allow you to adapt your studies to your personal situation, for example by combining studies with part-time work, delayed visa processes or managing individual circumstances.
In the later stages of the programme, you can specialise in up to two areas, such as Marketing & Sales, Finance & Accounting, or Digital Business & Information Systems, allowing you to shape your individual career path.
Throughout your studies, you benefit from a strong support system, including academic guidance, a buddy programme, and dedicated career services that support you from your first day until your career starts.
Start your career in Germany – study International Business now!
programmes.courseOrganisation:
In the Bachelor's programme in International Business, you will learn everything you need to understand international markets, think globally about business management issues, and act confidently in an intercultural environment. You will combine economic expertise with language skills and international perspectives.
At the same time, your studies should adapt to your life – not the other way around. Our updated curriculum offers flexibility, especially at the beginning of your studies. Hybrid learning elements in the early semesters allow you to stay on track even if your plans change, for example due to visa processes, travel delays, or other personal circumstances. This means you can follow courses from anywhere in the world for up to one full semester – or start your studies directly on campus and immerse yourself in student life from day one.
If you arrive on time, you will begin on campus with a strong foundation in languages and business basics before specialising in up to two areas such as Marketing & Sales, Finance & Accounting, Entrepreneurship & Sustainability, or Leadership & Organisational Development.
If your visa is delayed or you need more time to find accommodation in Weiden, you can start your studies in a hybrid format and transition to campus later without losing time.
programmes.internships: An internship with a duration of at least 20 weeks (full-time employment) in a company/institution in Germany or abroad is integrated in the study programme (sixth semester). The department staff supports the students in finding an internship.
programmes.partTimeJobs:
Several internationally operating companies are located in Weiden, which regularly offer internships and working student activities.
The curriculum also gives students the opportunity to work part-time.
OTH PartnerCircle supports a good partnership between university and industry. You may find suitable part-time employment here.
In general, part-time jobs can be found at "Hochschuljobboerse" – also for remote work.

programmes.description:
The vision of the International Business Bachelor's programme is to develop the most passionate leaders of tomorrow. The aim of the programme is to prepare students for the professional challenges of globally operating businesses.
The Bachelor’s programme in International Business provides a solid foundation in economics and business administration, with a strong focus on international contexts. It addresses the current demands of globally operating companies and emphasises the ability to solve complex economic challenges in an international and sustainable manner.
An integrated semester abroad offers valuable international experience and helps develop essential intercultural and social skills – key qualifications for a successful career in international environments.
programmes.courseOrganisation: The first two years (first to fourth semesters) comprise studies at TH Köln in the fields of international business administration, economics, law, and quantitative methods as well as intercultural competences. The fifth semester, the semester abroad, provides the opportunity to deepen certain course areas and expand the intercultural experience. During their sixth semester at TH Köln, students will finish their studies and write their Bachelor's thesis (180 ECTS). Students have the option to complete an optional seventh semester, a practical training semester abroad, and finish their Bachelor's degree with 210 ECTS.
programmes.internships: The seventh semester is an optional practical training semester abroad. Students may write their Bachelor's theses in cooperation with an international company.
programmes.partTimeJobs:
Taking on a part-time job while studying has lots of benefits. Students can earn some extra money and gain valuable professional experience, and they might even take a first step up on the career ladder. Gaining a first insight into the German corporate world is especially beneficial for international students.
Many students partially fund their studies at TH Köln by taking on a part-time job in or outside the university.
Please note that student jobs may require German language skills depending on the field and type of job.
Students who wish to pursue a career in Germany can take part in TH Köln's "Ready, Study, Go" programme. The programme offers students useful workshops and activities to prepare them for the German labour market.
programmes.accommodation:
Being Germany's fourth largest city, Cologne is a highly attractive place to live. The increasing influx of people can make the search for adequate accommodation quite difficult. Dozens of apartment hunters often compete for one single apartment. This is why we strongly recommend that you start looking for a place to live as soon as possible.
Cologne's most convenient and economical housing option is often a student dormitory. A public student services association called "Kölner Studierendenwerk" (KSTW) operates 88 student dorms offering roughly 4,800 rooms. The seemingly large number of dorm rooms is misleading; as the dormitories are open to the roughly 90,000 students enrolled at all Cologne universities, they are in extremely high demand. Please be aware that TH Köln does not allocate the rooms in these dorms. Please apply directly to the KSTW: https://www.kstw.de/wohnen. You do not yet need a letter of admission in order to apply.
The fierce competition in the private housing market has resulted in above-market rents – particularly in proximity to the city centre. We therefore encourage you to be flexible. Try to look for apartments outside the centre or share an apartment – and the cost of rent – with other students: www.th-koeln.de/accommodation.

programmes.description:
The study programme in International Business (BSc) develops the students' understanding of international business in a globalised world. Based on the latest theoretical concepts of business administration, the programme will equip students with the key business skills to work successfully in an international business environment. Furthermore, the programme offers a range of specialisations that will allow students to deepen their knowledge and meet their individual goals. Students can also participate in specialisations offered at partner universities worldwide. Selected lectures within the study programme include the following:
• Intercultural Communication
• International Business Law
• International Financial Accounting / Taxes
• Corporate Management
• Language courses
• International Management (specialisation)
Furthermore, the study programme includes an extended "mobility window" of three semesters between the fifth and the seventh semesters, during which the students have the chance to study abroad, complete an internship abroad, or write their final thesis abroad.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
In the first three semesters of the programme, the students participate in basic lectures in business administration and economics. Furthermore, the students learn another foreign language and explore how to communicate in an intercultural context.
The specialisations will be offered in the fourth and fifth semester. Students can choose specialisations offered at the Hochschule Bonn-Rhein-Sieg or one of the partner universities worldwide.
The following specialisations are offered locally at the moment:
• International Management
• Business-to-Business Marketing
• International Financial Management
• Sales Management
• Sustainability Management
• Marketing (in German)
• Controlling, Economics (in German)
• Health Management ("Gesundheitsmanagement" in German)
• Human Resources Management ("Personalmanagement" in German)
• Business Information Systems ("Wirtschaftsinformatik" in German)
• Logistics and Supply Chain Management (in German)
• Campus Rheinbach: Business Consulting and Development ("Unternehmensberatung und -entwicklung" in German), Accounting and Controlling (in German), Trade Management ("Handelsmanagement" in German)
In the sixth semester, the students have the option to complete an internship in Germany or abroad or to study abroad, for example, at one of the partner universities. The internship comprises a minimum of 20 weeks (full-time employment).
In the last semester of the programme, the students have to write a final thesis (duration: three months) and complete a colloquium. The thesis can be written in cooperation with a partner university or in cooperation with a company in Germany or abroad.
programmes.internships: An internship of at least 20 weeks duration (full-time employment) in a company/institution in Germany or abroad is integrated in the study programme (sixth semester). The department staff supports the students in finding an internship.
programmes.partTimeJobs: Many companies in the vicinity of Sankt Augustin, Bonn, and Cologne offer student jobs. However, please be advised that student visas restrict the number of hours that a student may work. Please be aware that for most jobs, a good proficiency in German is advantageous.
programmes.accommodation: Unlike in many other countries, German universities do not automatically provide their students with accommodation. Instead, students must make their own housing arrangements based on their own taste and requirements. There is a variety of options in Bonn or near the campuses in Sankt Augustin and Rheinbach, ranging from dormitories to privately arranged flat shares. For further information, please refer to the website of the International Welcome Centre: http://www.h-brs.de/en/accommodation-international-students and the accommodation website of the students' union Bonn: https://www.studierendenwerk-bonn.de/en/accommodation/

programmes.description:
The Master in International Business and Consulting - Strategic Management at HWR Berlin (Berlin School of Economics and Law) is designed for graduates from Germany and abroad who have completed a first university degree (usually a Bachelor's degree) and would like to study for a postgraduate degree in an international group of students.
The programme prepares students for positions which require strategic, cross-functional competencies in companies who are active in the international arena, in consulting firms, or in international investment promotion bodies. This may concern for instance internal and external project management and consulting roles, team membership in strategy and change projects, and assistant positions to executives with global responsibilities.
Courses are predominately structured as interactive seminars and are taught in English. Teaching takes place in seminars in which students have close contact with the teaching staff and in which they are expected to play an active part.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The Master's programme is divided into three parts:
• First semester: foundational courses and specialisation
• Second semester: foundational courses and specialisation
• Third semester: Master's thesis (provided students do not take an additional internship semester)
The first semester modules are worth a total of 30 credit points. During the first semester, students extend their knowledge in particular areas and commence their specialisation.
The second semester modules - also worth 30 credit points - build on the first semester to provide additional specialised skills required for challenges in their future careers.
The two semesters are accompanied by a personal development module which provides a platform for individual self-reflection and competence development.
For students who do not take an internship semester (usually students with 210 credit points), the third semester is scheduled for completing the degree by submitting a Master's thesis and defending it in an oral exam. During the third semester, a research methodology seminar is provided to support work on the Master's thesis. The third semester is worth a total of 30 credit points.
Total credits after successful completion of the programme: 90 ECTS
programmes.internships: For admission to the programme, 210 ECTS credit points are required. Applicants with 180 ECTS credit points will then be required to obtain the additional 30 ECTS credit points, for example, by completing an internship in the third semester. The programme will then last four semesters.
programmes.partTimeJobs: There are many job opportunities for students in Berlin. Non-EU students are permitted to work within specified limits.

programmes.description:
What you learn matters. Today's business world operates at the intersection of human leadership and digital innovation. Taught entirely in English, this programme equips you for a successful career in this modern landscape. You will build a comprehensive skill set across three core streams:
• Business management: Developing proficiency in international business, management science, and economics
• Data-based decision-making: Combining financial literacy, quantitative methods, and computing skills
• Future-shaping expertise: Exploring entrepreneurship, organisational development, and human-centred leadership, while customising your path through flexible electives
This programme goes beyond the broad foundations of up-to-date business management — it prepares you for the transition into professional life after graduation.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
How you learn makes all the difference — especially in a time shaped by AI, digital transformation, and rapidly changing careers. You will build a strong foundation on campus, test your skills in authentic business settings, and ultimately thrive in real-world practice. This is our RI5E2IMPACT approach: five semesters on campus, two in the world.
• Semesters one and two: Seed your success by experiencing business essentials through early management endeavours, building networks with international peers, and engaging with hands-on projects.
• Semesters three, four and five: Grow by deepening your management knowledge and applying your skills to authentic business scenarios, company-based case studies, simulations, and practitioner missions, while flexible electives let you shape your own path.
• Semesters six and seven: Flourish and create impact in the world. Spend semester six either studying abroad at a partner university, with the opportunity to earn a double degree, or gaining hands-on industry experience. Semester seven is completed fully online, allowing you to stay exactly where your career begins.
The programme combines academic rigour, international exposure, and practical relevance. We do not just teach theory — we bridge the gap between the classroom and the workplace. Make your mark where your career begins.

programmes.description:
The International Business Administration (IBA) Bachelor's programme offers you the opportunity to study at a young and modern university with an international orientation and to learn, live and develop personally together with people from more than 40 nations. Our aim is to offer you an international and interdisciplinary study programme at a high academic level that prepares you for the demands of an international job market. Our more than 290 partner universities, which not only enable you to spend an integrated period of study abroad, but also to take part in attractive dual programmes with our partner universities, play a key role in this.
Studying at Viadrina provides you with more than just the standard economics knowledge. Viadrina's location makes it an ideal place to acquire knowledge and skills in a European context, which will open up attractive career prospects for you, e.g. in European companies or European institutions. Living and studying simultaneously in two countries, Poland and Germany — studying at the renowned Faculty of Business Administration and Economics makes it possible.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
Basic studies
The basic studies modules are for orientation and provide the basis for the further study. The modules in this section are usually completed within the first three semesters.
• Business Informatics
• Business Taxation
• Finance & Investments
• Financial Accounting
• International Management
• Macroeconomics
• Management Accounting
• Marketing
• Mathematics
• Microeconomics
• Production & Logistics
• Statistics
Specialisation
The second phase of your studies (fourth to sixth semester) is dedicated to creating a profile. Within the context of focus area education, students deepen their knowledge in up to three of the offered majors dependent on the study programme. Available are:
• Accounting
• Banking and Finance
• Business & Economics in Central and Eastern Europe
• Economics
• Information & Operations Management
• Management, Marketing & Entrepreneurship
• Quantitative Methods
• Taxation
International orientation
Students must complete a semester of at least three months at a foreign university in the second stage of their studies. With a network of over 290 partner universities worldwide, the university actively supports you in planning and organising a study visit to a foreign university.
The opportunity to acquire a double degree is possible with a select group of partner universities. We currently maintain double degree programmes with:
• Universidad Católica de Cordoba (ARG)
• ICN École de Management, Nancy (FR)
• École Supérieure de Commerce de Montpellier (FR)
• Toulouse Business School (FR)
• University of Vaasa (FIN)
• Warsaw School of Economics (PL)
Bachelor's thesis and final colloquium
In the Bachelor thesis, students demonstrate that they are able to independently apply scientific methods and write texts in their field of study that meet academic requirements. Additionally, the oral exam is specifically designed to assess the student's ability to independently apply the scholarly methods used in the thesis.

programmes.description:
This consecutive Master's degree programme is a more research-oriented Master of Science programme, which provides theoretical knowledge and, in particular, methodological skills enabling students to independently expand their scientific knowledge. Research methods and strategies play a central role in the course content. In this way, the Master's programme not only prepares students for a professional career, but also for an academic career.
The programme consists of modules and is offered in several different study options. The different study options allow the students to specialise according to their individual interests. The faculty has introduced five different tracks (areas of specialisation). The standard duration of study is four semesters. The programme comprises 120 ECTS credits (hereinafter referred to as credits). The indicative study plans provide examples of a sensible structure for the degree programme (see annexes to the study-specific regulations).
In line with the international orientation of the degree programme, students must complete a semester lasting at least three months at a foreign university in the second or third semester of their studies (study abroad).
International students with no knowledge of German receive integrated German language lessons at the Viadrina Language Centre and reach CEFR level B1 by the end of their studies.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The IBA Master's degree is offered in five alternative tracks: ATL, FACT, FINE, DSDS and M&M. For students who do not wish to specialise in any of these fields, the cross-sectional Master's programme (General Management) offers an alternative.
Accounting, Taxation & Law
The ATL track combines business, economics and law content and prepares students for these challenges. Whether group accounting & group auditing, taxation of mergers & acquisitions, or commercial and corporate law — the ATL track opens up excellent career prospects in diverse, attractive, and stable professional fields. The curriculum is supplemented by current and practice-relevant topics such as sustainability reporting, tax technology, and sustainable private and commercial law.
Finance, Accounting, Controlling & Taxation
The FACT track is aimed at students pursuing management positions at consulting firms, finance-oriented and capital market-oriented companies, or corporate controlling. The programme focuses on companies with an international orientation that are focused on Central and Eastern Europe.
Finance & International Economics
The FINE track aims to provide a holistic understanding of the common market and international trade, international financial markets, and European and international economic policy, especially monetary policy. Special attention is given to issues of European integration, European and international environmental and energy policy, international tax competition, and competition between social systems and their coordination in the EU.
Management & Marketing
The M&M track teaches the latest state of the theoretical discussion in the fields of management and marketing. It provides the participants with the necessary orientation that they will need in order to actively take part in shaping the changes driven by the globalisation of markets.
Data Science & Decision Support
Data is important for managing businesses at all levels and creating value for customers. However, humans are unable to oversee the vast amounts of data available, and it is becoming increasingly impossible to draw conclusions without the help of powerful tools. DSDS is the right track for students who wish to understand data models and artificial intelligence algorithms in order to make informed business decisions.

programmes.description:
The study programme in "International Business Administration" takes account of increasing globalisation and provides you with the competences you will need as a career starter in multinational companies.
Out of five specialisations ("Accounting, taxes and auditing", "Internal accounting"; "Human resources management", "Marketing" and "Logistics"), students can choose two of these specialisations, taking compulsory elective subjects. This allows students to provide their studies with an individual touch, based on their personal preference and subjects of interest.
During their university studies, students will spend a semester abroad to improve their foreign language skills and gain additional intercultural experience. The university studies programme prepares students to work in intercultural teams and deal with the special features of different national markets.
The Bachelor's degree in International Business Administration has a long tradition at the Fulda University of Applied Sciences. It has a strong international and applied focus. It extends over seven semesters and 35 modules and comprises a compulsory semester abroad, which is completed in the form of a period of study abroad or a work placement module in a foreign language.
The aim of the study programme is to provide students with comprehensive knowledge of the most important contents, methods, concepts and instruments of general business administration, operational functions and related disciplines and to enable them to use these in familiar and new tasks of theoretical and practical business administration work in an international context. Students benefit from small course sizes and experience internationality through the multicultural composition of the student groups.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
In the first two semesters, you will primarily familiarise yourself with the basics of business administration and law. You will also learn important mathematics basics and techniques for academic research.
In the third and fourth semesters, you will then gain insights into the business management functions of an enterprise, supplemented by further economics and legal aspects.
You will also acquire English skills at an academic level and you will learn how to use application software to support the resource planning of an enterprise.
Internship/ semester abroad (fifth semester):
In the fifth semester, you complete either a study abroad programme at a foreign university or a work placement module (BPS) in an enterprise based abroad. Alternatively, the work placement module can also be carried out in an international division of an enterprise based in Germany.
The condition for the semester abroad is that you must have successfully completed the modules of the first and second semesters and earned 75 ECTS credits by 15 April or by 15 October before the start of your university studies / internship.
Profile programme (sixth and seventh semester):
You design your profile studies according to your interests by choosing a specialisation from the following offer – consisting of three subject-related modules – in order to deepen your knowledge in these. You supplement this specialisation with two compulsory elective subjects, which will give your university studies a very individual grade. You will also acquire specialisation in business management and use the knowledge you have acquired in the previous semesters in a practical business simulation.
programmes.internships: The internship to be completed as part of the work placement module is an alternative to the period of study abroad. It lasts six months, has an international focus and is completed at a location of an enterprise or organisation in a foreign language country. The usual working hours of a full-time employee apply.
programmes.partTimeJobs: From tutoring jobs and student assistantships at Fulda University to typical student jobs in restaurants, shops, and many other industries in the city of Fulda and its surrounding area, a wide range of job opportunities is available. Please note that proficiency in German significantly increases employability.
programmes.accommodation:
The International Office offers an accommodation service for international students coming directly from abroad. The cost of accommodation amounts to approx. 400 to 500 EUR per month. There are excellent, newly built student residences within walking distance of the university.
For more information on housing, see: https://www.hs-fulda.de/en/international/international-students/housing.

programmes.description:
ENTREPRENEURIAL ACTIVITIES IN A RESPONSIBLE MANNER
The Bachelor's programme in International Business Administration and Entrepreneurship is based on a broad, basic, academic education.
In this programme, you will receive training in the functional areas of business, allowing you to develop important managerial and entrepreneurial skills. These skills are necessary for success in a rapidly changing business environment. Special emphasis is placed on management and entrepreneurial orientation from an international perspective.
The knowledge of entrepreneurship in theory and practice, business processes, and management functions is complemented by further broader specific areas such as accounting, finance, marketing, law, psychology, organisational behaviour, IT, and qualitative and quantitative research methods.
Furthermore, through a historical view of management as well as a study of corporate and business ethics issues, you will develop a historically embedded and society oriented perspective. This should sensitise you not only to take responsibility in your field of business but also for society and the environment as well.
As a student of International Business Administration & Entrepreneurship at Leuphana, you can also apply for a double degree programme at the University of Glasgow in Finance, Business Economics, or Business Management.

STUDYING AT LEUPHANA UNIVERSITY OF LÜNEBURG
This Bachelor's degree programme at Leuphana University of Lüneburg consists of four basic elements: the International Business Administration and Entrepreneurship major (90 ECTS credits), the minor (30 ECTS credits), the Leuphana Semester (30 ECTS credits), and the Complementary Studies (30 ECTS credits).
The Bachelor's degree programme in International Business Administration and Entrepreneurship begins with the Leuphana Semester, during which you will learn the methodological and disciplinary foundations of your academic specialisation in international business administration. From the second semester, your Bachelor's programme is divided into International Business Administration and the Entrepreneurship major, a minor of your choice (e.g. Economics, Popular Music Studies, Philosophy, or Sustainability Science), and Complementary Studies. In the Complementary Studies, you can try out new ways of working and thinking from other disciplines, allowing you to expand your interdisciplinary skills.

programmes.description:
The World of Business from a Global Perspective
Kick-start your international career with our Bachelor in Business Administration – entirely in English!
This isn’t just another degree. It's your gateway to a world of opportunities. Our English-language Bachelor’s programme in Business Administration is designed to launch your career, both locally and internationally.
Our approach to learning
Comprehensive Knowledge: Discover much more than just the basics of business administration! Grasp global economic dynamics, prepare for entrepreneurship, learn to collaborate effectively in teams, and sharpen your presentation skills.
Hands-On Learning: At our university, theory meets practice. Through projects, presentations, and real-world applications, we ensure you’re well-prepared for the job market.
Methodological Competence: We teach you the skills you’ll need to tackle new topics independently – a crucial asset in any future role.
Digital Readiness: With cutting-edge tools and technologies, we equip you for tomorrow’s digital economy. You’ll also gain valuable expertise in using artificial intelligence tools in business contexts.
Global Outlook: We keep a close eye on the fast-moving international business landscape, preparing you to handle challenges on a global scale.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
Programme Breakdown
First semesters: Your will kick off with “Freshers’ Week” – a great chance to meet fellow students (around 50% international) and get all the information you need. Lectures start with “Fundamentals of Business Administration”, giving you a solid overview of the business world. In the following semesters, you'll build on this with core subjects like Marketing, Strategic Management, Human Resources, and Accounting. You’ll also cover Economics and International Business Law. In Business Mathematics and Statistics, you’ll gain essential data analysis and numerical reasoning skills – always with a practical focus.
Elective modules: In semesters four and five, you can tailor your studies by choosing six modules from a pool of 15 courses, e.g.
• Trend Research
• Business Ethics
• Digital Technology and Data Analytics
• Consumer Psychology
• SAP – Enterprise Resource Planning Systems
• Design Thinking
• Political Economy
• Language course
Business and more: This programme goes beyond academics. With modules like “Communication and Cooperation”, “Project Management”, and “Corporate Social Responsibility”, you’ll build key soft skills. Teaching is modern and interactive – for example, simulating a company’s supply chain with Lego to better understand logistics.
Practical experience: Throughout the programme, you’ll work on real-life projects. In the “Entrepreneurship and Business Planning” module, you and your team develop a business idea, pitch it to external experts, and create a detailed business plan. In your fifth semester, all students collaborate on “Interdisciplinary Projects,” working with peers from other disciplines. These projects are often initiated by regional companies, associations, or civil society organisations. You might, for example, team up with psychologists and designers to create a marketing strategy and materials, or assess a recycling initiative using an app developed by IT students.
Expand your horizons: In the sixth semester, you can choose to study abroad or complete an internship – both excellent ways to apply your knowledge in an international context.
Highly motivated? If you’re particularly driven, you can take part in an exciting opportunity to study at our partner university, Fitchburg State University near Boston, and earn both a Bachelor of Arts from us and a Bachelor of Science from them. You’ll spend your fifth and sixth semesters in the US, and upon successful completion, you will be able to obtain two prestigious degrees.
programmes.internships:
An eight-week internship has to be completed before the start of the fourth semester. You can also do this internship in your home country before applying to Rhine-Waal University of Applied Sciences.
In the sixth semester, students have the chance to either study abroad or do a 20-week internship (in Germany or abroad). We provide support in selecting partner universities and institutions as well as in raising funds.

Student jobs within the university can be solely in English, but the vast majority of off-campus jobs will require at least basic proficiency in German. German courses are available for students through our International Center.
First-year students are strongly advised to focus primarily on their studies and to begin learning German. This will open up many more part-time job opportunities in later semesters.
programmes.accommodation:
Rhine-Waal University of Applied Sciences strongly urges you to arrange your accommodation before arrival. One option is accommodation at the residence halls run by student services ("Studierendenwerk Düsseldorf") with one-, two- or three-room flats and rent starting around 290 EUR per month (with a security deposit equivalent to three months' rent). Availability is limited, so register online as soon as possible. See our website for details.
Most students live in private flats shared with other students. There are a number of popular online portals for finding a flat in Germany. Contact the Welcome Centre for more information or look into social media platforms because some students might be graduating when you plan to start. Additionally, the Welcome Centre is always ready to offer advice or help with conversations or correspondence in German.

programmes.description:
The Bachelor’s programme in International Business and Economics offers a unique combination of economics and business administration with a strong international and quantitative focus. It is designed for students who want to understand how global markets work and how firms make strategic decisions in a complex economic environment.
A key strength of the programme is its emphasis on analytical and quantitative skills. Students learn how to work with data, apply econometric methods, and develop evidence-based solutions to real-world economic and business challenges. This skill set is highly valued in today’s increasingly data-driven global economy.
By integrating perspectives from economics and management, the programme provides a comprehensive understanding of the interaction between firms, markets, and public policy.
The programme is taught entirely in English and includes the study of an additional foreign language, including German studies for internationals. Students benefit from an international classroom, close interaction with faculty, and excellent opportunities to gain international experience through partner universities and internships.
Graduates are well equipped for international careers in consulting, finance, public institutions, and global companies, or for pursuing a Master’s degree at leading universities worldwide.
IBE Module Descriptions
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The International Business and Economics programme consists of a sequence of required courses of an economic and managerial nature, with a theoretical, analytical, and interculturally oriented approach.
The programme comprises two parts: compulsory modules and compulsory elective modules. Compulsory studies start from the first semester and go through the fourth semester. Modules offered: Micro- and Macroeconomics, Principles of Management, Financial Accounting, Statistics, Game Theory, Mathematical Methods, Marketing Performance Management, Financial Management, Decision & Strategy, International Economics, Economic Policy, Econometrics, Principles of International Management, Productions, Logistics and Management Science, English at an academic level, a second foreign language, and German (DAF) for international students.
Students will specialise during their fifth and sixth semesters by choosing compulsory elective courses in international business or global economics, including a project seminar. These compulsory electives can also be taken at a cooperating partner institution abroad. Credits earned during the study abroad period will be recognised, and an advisory service is offered. A special feature at our school is the so-called CoMeT module. In this module, students may gain credits for their volunteer work by applying business and economics skills at one of the student organisations at the university or in the city of Magdeburg. Special regulations will apply.
A written Bachelor's thesis and a corresponding seminar that includes a presentation will round off the undergraduate study programme.
Students should expect a weekly workload of approx. 20 hours of classroom studies and at least 20 hours of independent self-study in our full-time study programme. Forms of classroom instruction include on-campus lectures, tutorials, and seminars.
To assist students during the study programme, the faculty provides academic Bachelor's advisory services.
programmes.internships: There are no integrated internships during the Bachelor's studies, as we are focusing on research methods. However, students are highly encouraged to complete a self-organised internship at the end of their studies. The faculty believes it is valuable to gain professional experience within German and international workplaces. Internships must be organised independently https://www.isp.ovgu.de/IBEApplication.html. Furthermore, student organisations, such as AIESEC, Enactus, and others, are active on campus. These organisations and the University Career Service Centre provide opportunities and assistance to both German and international students.
programmes.accommodation:
The "Studentenwerk" (student union) in Magdeburg manages the on-campus halls of residence (mostly one- to four-room apartments). Currently, the monthly rent ranges from 200 EUR to 500 EUR per room (approx. 12 to 35 square meters), depending on the size and furnishing. Rooms in the halls of residence are limited in number. The accommodation application can be found on the website of the Studentenwerk.
The Studentenwerk assists all new students in finding adequate accommodation, either on or off campus. Private accommodation is available on the Magdeburg accommodation market. However, fully furnished units are in somewhat short supply.

programmes.description:
The Master's programme in International Business and Global Transformation offers opportunities for you to broaden the knowledge acquired during your previous undergraduate studies in International Business, as well as any professional experience you may have gained thereafter. The programme is designed to provide an application-oriented approach to teaching and learning, encompassing five module categories: core curriculum, quantitative methods, laboratories, personal skills development programme, and the final exam period, which includes the Master's thesis and colloquium. Case studies, business simulation games, e-learning modules, interactive training sessions, and regular feedback will assist you in the practical application and integration of your individual skills.
You will acquire extensive, up-to-date knowledge of all relevant aspects of international business, with a particular focus on key aspects relating to sustainability. Sustainability, in its various dimensions, is at the very core of the Master's programme in International Business and Global Transformation, serving as a strategic foundation for learning about responsible management assessment, problem-solving, and decision-making in a sustainable manner.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The first year (first and second semesters) comprises of studies at TH Köln in Cologne, Germany. In the second year (third semester), students spend a mandatory semester abroad. In the fourth semester, students write their Master's theses, which may be prepared in cooperation with an international company or organisation. The programme concludes with a colloquium upon successful completion of the thesis. Students are encouraged to complete an internship at companies or organisations during the summer and winter breaks.
Alongside their studies, students have many opportunities to demonstrate their social responsibility and commitment as well as to improve their knowledge. Active communities on campus include the departmental student representatives of business administration studies (Fachschaft Wirtschaft, http://www.fachschaft-wirtschaft.info), the student union (AStA, http://www.asta.th-koeln.de), and many other student initiatives, such as the Faculty Alumni Association, Marketing zwischen Theorie und Praxis e.V. (MTP), and Enactus.
programmes.internships: Students may write their Master's theses in cooperation with an international company or organisation.
programmes.partTimeJobs:
Taking on a part-time job while studying has lots of benefits. Students can earn some extra money and gain valuable professional experience, and they might even take a first step up on the career ladder. Gaining a first insight into the German corporate world is especially beneficial for international students.
Many students partially fund their studies at TH Köln by taking on a part-time job in or outside the university.
Please note that student jobs may require German language skills depending on the field and type of job.
Students who wish to pursue a career in Germany can take part in TH Köln's "Ready, Study, Go" programme. The programme offers students useful workshops and activities to prepare them for the German labour market.
programmes.accommodation:
Being Germany's fourth largest city, Cologne is a highly attractive place to live. The increasing influx of people can make the search for adequate accommodation quite difficult. Dozens of apartment hunters often compete for one single apartment. This is why we strongly recommend that you start looking for a place to live as soon as possible.
Cologne's most convenient and economical housing option is often a student dormitory. A public student services association called "Kölner Studierendenwerk" (KSTW) operates 88 student dorms offering roughly 4,800 rooms. The seemingly large number of dorm rooms is misleading; as the dormitories are open to the roughly 90,000 students enrolled at all Cologne universities, they are in extremely high demand. Please be aware that TH Köln does not allocate the rooms in these dorms. Please apply directly to the KSTW: https://www.kstw.de/wohnen. You do not yet need a letter of admission in order to apply.
The fierce competition in the private housing market has resulted in above-market rents – particularly in proximity to the city centre. We therefore encourage you to be flexible. Try to look for apartments outside the centre or share an apartment – and the cost of rent – with other students: www.th-koeln.de/accommodation.

programmes.description:
The MSc in International Business and Intercultural Management comprises three major stages:
The programme starts with an induction period and foundation stage, during which students assess their current level of subject knowledge. Students will gain sound insights into internal and external business environments. They will further deepen their knowledge of internal company processes, specifically in human resource management and leadership, global marketing, and international finance and economics. Intercultural communication will be thoroughly addressed during this stage, as it remains a major challenge in corporate entities.
Semester two offers advanced studies in intercultural management and the business environment. Adopting a cross-disciplinary approach, this phase offers students the opportunity to broaden their expertise in the business environment while enabling them to focus their studies in areas of personal interest.
Semester three is the Master's thesis stage, which requires in-depth empirical research in each student's chosen area. Ideally, the thesis is based on real situations in international companies or organisations, with a focus on sustainability / corporate responsibility. During the first two semesters, this programme offers various courses on quantitative and qualitative research, which will prepare students for this stage.
Students also have the possibility to integrate an internship or a study abroad semester into their Master's studies. If they choose to take advantage of these opportunities in the third semester, the Master's thesis will be completed in a fourth semester.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
Students experience a period of intensive independent study. This allows them to progress at a speed suited to their individual needs and to work on their own initiatives in areas which are of interest and value to them. Some more specific objectives of this approach are:
• to introduce students to the techniques of researching, organising, and presenting the results of their work
• to stimulate critical thinking and logical analysis
• to develop a sense of responsibility for attaining their goals and to increase and foster consciousness regarding sustainability issues
The course content is founded on a sound theoretical basis and includes experience-based and hands-on forms of learning, such as guided business simulations, case studies, project work, and role plays.
A tutorial support service is offered for students on both an individual and a group basis.

programmes.description:
Locations: Dresden and Heidelberg
Our International Business and Leadership Master's programme will enable you to start your career in multinational companies or to build up your own business. Study in our Management and Leadership programme and experience international exchange in various ways, including cultural diversity in class, a curriculum with a purely international focus, and a semester abroad at one of our partner universities.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The duration of the Master's degree programme is 24 months. The degree programme is divided into five-week blocks. There is an exam for each module in the fifth week. This ensures that competencies are acquired in a focused way. There are no semesters or trimesters (terms) as such. The programme contents are conveyed by means of case studies or project-based applications and include an integrated study abroad period.
Courses in the first academic year include the following:
• Strategy
• Marketing and Sales Management
• Economics of globalisation
• Current Topic
• Leadership
• Business Research Methods
• Accounting
• Financial Management: Controlling and Corporate Finance
• Entrepreneurship
In the second year, students study abroad and write their Master's theses.
The small student groups (maximum 25 students), the mentoring system, and the open-door policy as well as the renowned, experienced teaching staff guarantee special and very individual study conditions and attention.
The programme can also be studies with a duration of three semesters.
programmes.internships: Participants can spend the third semester doing an internship in Germany or abroad.
programmes.partTimeJobs:
Working as a non-EU citizen: In possession of a valid German residence permit for study purposes, you are allowed to work for up to 120 full days (full day = eight hours per day) or 240 half days (half day = four hours) during the calendar year. However, freelance work is not permitted. Internships that are mandatory for the successful completion of your studies at SRH do not count towards the above-named 120 full days.
Employment that is considered “student part-time work” ("studentische Nebentätigkeit", e.g. employment as a student worker at a university or in a university-related organisation or "Werkstudent" activities at companies that are related to your studies) can be done without any time restrictions.

programmes.description:
The consecutive, English-taught Master's programme in International Business and Management (IBM) builds up on the business knowledge students previously gained in related Bachelor's programmes and provides in-depth and up-to date knowledge of business studies and key qualifications in the area of international management. After their graduation, students have gained the requirements needed for employees in specialised and leading positions in international companies or organisations. Graduates are able to take over complex leadership tasks.
This is possible through the programme's intense relation to practical experience and focus on key challenges of international management at an advanced level. Combined with a high degree of internationality in the composition of the study group and the teaching content, students are well prepared to meet the challenges of a continuously changing international environment.
Teaching methods include lectures, case studies, management simulations, team work, project work, presentations and assignments. Interaction between students and lecturers is fostered in small groups, which provide the opportunity for discussions about the issues at stake. Both teamwork in small international study groups and individual study are applied throughout the studies.
Studying International Business and Management at Osnabrück University of Applied Sciences also includes:
• small class size, close contact between students and teaching staff
• international study groups
• intensive training of social and intercultural skills
• balance between theory and practical contents
• highly qualified lecturers with profound management experience
• face-to-face lectures, seminars, project work, e-learning
• intensive and individual counselling and coaching before and during studies
• buddy system
• European Credit Transfer System (ECTS)
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The Master's programme in International Business and Management is designed as a full-time programme that combines intensive classroom study with a demanding independent study programme. The curriculum comprises 120 ECTS.
During the first, second, and third semesters, students take six courses representing 30 ECTS credits per semester. Out of these six courses, three courses belong to the key competence (international business management), one course belongs to the general competences (social skills, communication, and research methods), and two courses belong to the two individually chosen electives. Each course in either category is worth five ECTS credits. Courses are usually given as lectures, and a schedule for each semester is fixed by the university. During the fourth semester, students write their Master's theses. The thesis represents 30 ECTS credits.
For more information on the study outline and for the module handbook, please see the structure of the programme.

If you speak German well enough, there are many job opportunities in Osnabrück in bakeries, supermarkets, industry, restaurants, etc.
For international degree-seeking students, the university also has a career service that assists you with application checks, contacts to companies and more. Mrs Laetitia Godineau will answer your questions around finding a job during your studies as well as about making the transition into the job market after graduation.
Important: If you need to work to support yourself, you should start looking for a student job as early as possible.

Important: Apply for accommodation as soon as you apply for a place on a programme, as you don't have to submit the university's letter of admission at the beginning of the application process. This is the best advice we can give you, and it has worked for many others.
Need more advice? Just contact the Center for International Students at international@hs-osnabrueck.de.

programmes.description:
The Bachelor's programme in International Business and Management prepares you for a career in national or international companies. The programme is taught in German and English, includes a semester abroad and practice-oriented projects, and allows you to choose your own specialisation.
Language Policy
Lectures in the first two semesters are conducted in German; some of them can be replaced by English‑taught classes. From the third semester onward, both German and English are used as languages of instruction. Business English is integrated as a first foreign language, and Spanish, French, Russian or Chinese can be selected as a second foreign language.
Competence Profile
You acquire comprehensive knowledge and competencies in all areas of business management and, after completing the Bachelor's degree, you can work as a junior manager in companies or organisations. You will learn to act in the interest of sustainable value creation and to develop solutions collaboratively for global enterprises.
Didactic Concept
The teaching content is delivered in German and English within small, international study groups. The programme offers opportunities to gain cross-cultural competencies during your studies and to establish contacts worldwide.
Specialisation and Language Options
You can select among various specialisations in business management, economics and business languages, study additional foreign languages, and gain experience abroad.
Study‑Abroad Semester
A semester abroad, usually taken in the fifth semester, is a compulsory, integrated part of the programme. Around 150 partner universities worldwide are available, and the semester abroad may also be undertaken at a non-partner university. One or more additional semesters or study stays abroad are possible.
Double-Degree Options
With a French and a South Korean university, double-degree agreements are in place; after a one-year study period at those institutions you can also obtain the Bachelor’s degree awarded by these institutions.
Practical Relevance and Professional Field
Practice-oriented projects, the integrated semester abroad and work in small, diverse groups strengthen both your professional and intercultural competence. In an increasingly globalised world, professionals with these skills are in high demand. Your knowledge of international markets and sustainable value creation will help you develop innovative solutions for the economic challenges of tomorrow.

The programme includes a Personal Development Journey throughout the entire course of study: Through intensive block seminars, you will further develop personal and interpersonal skills and acquire the competencies to become a responsible leader.

programmes.description:
Our economy is increasingly determined by globalisation. German companies in nearly all branches operate internationally at this point. Are you interested in a career at the international level? Then earn your degree in our English-taught undergraduate Bachelor's programme in International Business and Management and obtain the qualifications you will need for your professional future.
Our degree programme places immense importance on practice-oriented teaching and application. Over the course of your studies, you will build a solid theoretical foundation in business administration, economics and management, while also learning how to effectively apply your know-how and skills for practical purposes through numerous projects with (supra-)regional companies and partner universities in Germany and abroad. Approachable professors with extensive industry experience will be guiding you along the way.
During your studies, you will develop an array of key skills, including how to conduct research, entrepreneurial thinking and interpersonal skills that are indispensable in the modern workplace. Through various forms of exams, such as group presentations, you will be given numerous opportunities to improve your public speaking abilities, confidence and professional communication skills as well as your teamwork and conflict management skills. And if you are interested in obtaining further qualifications, consider earning a double degree in business with our partner university abroad.
At Rhine-Waal University of Applied Sciences, you will work, study and interact with colleagues in English in a deeply international environment, allowing you to improve your language proficiency and experience other cultures organically as you earn your degree.
What are you waiting for? Let us prepare you for your professional career in international business and management together.
programmes.courseOrganisation: In total, the standard period of study comprises seven semesters of study. Additionally, sound foundations in business administration and economics are imparted, as are analytical skills and fundamental knowledge of social sciences. This acquired knowledge is then enhanced in key areas in the fourth and fifth semesters. The sixth semester is reserved for a practical internship or semester abroad. Through the choice of specific elective subjects and the organisation of the sixth semester, students can sharpen their profile in terms of their aspired careers after graduation. In the final semester, each student writes a Bachelor's thesis after having developed an appropriate topic.
programmes.internships:
An eight-week internship has to be completed before the start of the fourth semester. You can also do this internship in your home country before applying to Rhine-Waal University of Applied Sciences.
The sixth semester is reserved for an internship or a semester abroad.
programmes.partTimeJobs:
Non-EU students can work up to 120 full days or 240 half days per year without requiring an additional visa. Student jobs within the university can be solely in English, but the vast majority of off-campus jobs will require at least basic proficiency in German. German courses are available for students through our International Center.
First-year students are strongly advised to focus primarily on their studies and to begin learning German. This will open up many more part-time job opportunities in later semesters.
programmes.accommodation:
Rhine-Waal University of Applied Sciences strongly urges you to arrange your accommodation before arrival. One option is accommodation at the residence halls run by student services ("Studierendenwerk Düsseldorf") with one-, two- or three-room flats and rent starting around 290 EUR per month (with a security deposit equivalent to three months' rent). Availability is limited, so register online as soon as possible. See our website for details.
Most students live in private flats shared with other students. There are a number of popular online portals for finding a flat in Germany. Contact the Welcome Centre for more information or look into social media platforms because some students might be graduating when you plan to start. Additionally, the Welcome Centre is always ready to offer advice or help with conversations or correspondence in German.

programmes.description:
What kind of student are you?
• Do you have a professional interest in transition countries, emerging economies or less developed countries?
• Are you looking for additional academic challenges to improve your career prospects in the fields of international business and development economics?
• Are you interested in acquiring intercultural skills in these markets?
• Would you like to gain international experience during your studies?
• Are you ready to study in a challenging and competitive programme?
If the answers to these questions are positive, then this MBA programme is the right one for you!
We invite you to take a look at the structure and organisation of this unique study programme, which leverages the years of experience of our faculty at one of the oldest universities in the world and our hand-selected partner universities.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The Master's degree programme is an economics-oriented degree programme that offers students a modern education in the overlapping area of modern economics, in particular modern development economics and environmental economics, and business administration, in particular international management. These areas usually have a special connection to resource-related industries. The teaching modules are designed to enable students to develop a detailed and critical understanding of the particularities, limitations, terminologies, and doctrines in these areas, generating a particular understanding of the nuances of cooperation between Eastern, South-Eastern, and Western Europe and emerging Asian economies on the one hand, and the increasing importance of ecological interrelationships on the other.
Students thus acquire skills for dealing with new and unfamiliar complex tasks and problems in the areas of management of international companies, administrations, and international organisations. Using the theoretical framework they have acquired, they can develop and apply new ideas and procedures and evaluate them by taking into account different scientific standards of judgement. This enables them to develop strategic solutions even with incomplete information and weigh them up against each other in scenarios that allow students to independently manage processes in the strategy-orientated professional field of international management. In these fields of activity in particular, the requirements structure is characterised by frequent and unpredictable changes.
The interactive nature of the courses aims to help students develop their personal communication and cooperation skills in the fields that are decisive for the professional field. As a result, they will be able to integrate other participants into tasks in a goal-oriented manner within a management function, taking into account the respective group situation, deal constructively with conflicts, and define the expected social, economic, and cultural effects to integrate them into the decision-making process.
You will also receive tuition-free German language courses over the period of the first two semesters, and you can do an internship to earn credit points.
If you choose the International Business specialisation, you will have the opportunity to spend one semester abroad at one of our partner universities. We also have double degree agreements, which enable you to stay at a partner university for one year and earn two Master's degrees — one from each institution.
The taught modules include lectures, tutorials, practical exercises, case studies, and seminars.

programmes.description:
International Business and Technology (IBT) is a unique study combination of International Business, a technical specialisation (Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Natural Sciences), and two languages. After completing the regular study period of seven semesters (210 ECTS), students will have gained extensive knowledge of international business as well as knowledge in their field of technical specialisation. They will also have acquired transdisciplinary competencies.
The programme is bilingual. In the first two semesters, the courses are held in English. From the third semester onwards, students choose a technical specialisation, which can be either Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Natural Sciences. The language of instruction will be German.
In addition to the regular seven-semester International Business and Technology programme, we offer an eight-semester study option called International Business and Technology Plus (IBT Plus). This study option includes one compulsory year abroad, which consists of a 20-week international internship and a study semester at one of our partner universities. It is especially fitting for students who want to give the international component of their studies more importance.
The International Business and Technology programme offers a double degree with "Chinesisch Deutsche Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften" (CDHAW)/ Tongji University, Shanghai, China.
Graduates may work in a wide variety of positions located at the intersection of business and technology.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The seven-semester programme, conducted in English and German, blends business knowledge with engineering sciences, while promoting problem-solving and communication skills. With a Bachelor's degree in Engineering, you will be suited for management tasks in internationally active companies of all sizes. You can specialise e.g. in the purchase and sale of international high-tech products or work directly in product management. You can work in consulting, take responsibility for business transactions and participate in technical processes and developments. Opportunities are provided in project management at the interface of business and technology. You can also join the technical risk assessment team of banks and insurance companies. Manifold career opportunities will generally be open to you, as you will receive international training and acquire sound and comprehensive knowledge in technology, natural sciences, and economics.
As a student of International Business and Technology, you will learn the fundamentals of business administration and natural sciences and dive into the world of technology with your chosen specialisation in Mechanical Engineering (including engineering design, simulation, and manufacturing), Electrical Engineering (including digital electronics and data networks) or Natural Sciences (with a focus on physics, optimisation, and fundamentals of engineering design and electrical engineering).
You can find a sample study plan and information on all mandatory modules on our website.
For information on the additional semester featuring our IBT Plus study option, please visit our website.
Graduates of the programme are awarded the academic degree of Bachelor of Engineering (BEng).
programmes.internships: During the sixth and seventh semester, students complete a 16-week internship, either abroad or in Germany. This internship allows students to work alongside global managers, apply theoretical knowledge to real-world business scenarios, and develop practical and managerial skills. While organising an internship abroad can be challenging, our dedicated support ensures that you’re well-prepared for this transformative experience.

Part-time jobs outside the university are also available. Students can, for instance, have a "450 EUR job" or be employed as a working student in one of the companies in the Nuremberg region.
However, students should make sure that they have enough time to study.

programmes.courseOrganisation: You will have the opportunity to shape your study schedule from the start.
