programmes.description:
In this more application-oriented Master's degree the graduates continue their education in the fields of modern mathematics and learn in-depth scientific concepts, methods and techniques that enable the graduates to handle challenging and complex mathematical problems in applications.
The Master's programme is characterised by:
• scientific orientation
• concentration on the specialisations in "mathematics for sustainability", "business mathematics", and "mathematical data science"
• particular emphasis on practical relevance project orientation
• development and extension of capacity for teamwork, good organisational skills, and leadership skills, and
• the Master's thesis as an application-oriented scientific work
The graduates develop the following professional skills and competences: application of knowledge, methods and techniques from diverse subjects of mathematics on concrete problems (further elaboration in mathematical and scientific expertise, scientific working methods, problem-solving competence, and analytical mindset), quick familiarisation in new fields of application which provides experts with high-quality solutions (self-competence, critical thinking, ability to transfer established methods to new problems in practice), procedural approach based on project management methods to handle functional and organisational difficulties appearing in practical questions (organisational skills and social skills), communication skills and well-founded judgement in critical dialogue with experts in practice (communication skills and leadership skills as part of social competencies). These key qualifications empower the graduates to assume managerial positions and leadership responsibilities in the private as well as the public sector ("higher civil service"). Highly qualified graduates are prepared to enter a doctoral studies programme.

programmes.description:
The Master's programme in Mathematics in Data Science is oriented towards students seeking a high-profile education in Mathematics with a focus on the rapidly growing fields of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. Graduates of this programme will gain in-depth knowledge of advanced techniques for data analysis and processing, the ability to adapt complex models to real-world problems, and the skills to combine and refine these models to develop predictive and classification tools. Graduates will be qualified to assess different algorithms' capabilities and limits and to design effective solutions for specific problems.
The programme emphasises the mathematical foundations of methods and algorithms used in machine learning, statistics, optimisation, and data representation theory. It balances theoretical knowledge with practical applications in data analysis, data engineering, and machine learning.
In addition, students will take interdisciplinary classes, including foreign language training, introductory law courses, and lectures addressing the social and political dimensions of data science.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
This two-year, four-semester Master’s programme offers a rigorous foundation in the mathematical principles underlying data science -- including data acquisition, modelling, and classification. While the programme emphasises mathematical depth, it remains flexible, allowing you to tailor your studies to your specific interests within the field.
You will take part in lectures, hands-on practical courses, and seminars, and you will also have the chance to carry out your own research. In addition to core technical content, the curriculum thoughtfully integrates courses on the social and ethical dimensions of data handling, both within the main programme and through targeted elective options.
The programme culminates in a Master's thesis during the fourth semester, allowing you to apply your knowledge in a focused research project.

• Specialisation 30 to 51 CP
• Pure Mathematics 9 to 30 CP
• Applied Mathematics 18 to 30 CP

The academic year is divided into two semesters, a winter semester (1 October until 31 March) and a summer semester (1 April until 30 September). programmes.description: The Max Planck School Matter to Life offers an integrated MSc/PhD graduate programme. Students receive their joint Master's degree in Matter to Life by regularly studying at the two teaching universities (University of Göttingen or Heidelberg University). programmes.courseOrganisation:
The joint degree Master's programme will be spent at one of the following two teaching universities, depending on your choice of focus:
• Complex Systems and Biological Physics (University of Göttingen)
• Molecular Systems Chemistry and Engineering (Heidelberg University)
The universities share a core curriculum with classes taught in connected classrooms. Laboratory rotations at associated institutions during the Master's phase of the programme are encouraged and the students are supported in building their own research networks in this highly interdisciplinary area. All students are given a buddy and a mentor to guide them through the programme.
After you have successfully completed your Master's, you can continue with a three-year PhD programme under the supervision of one of the school's fellows.
Voluntary preparatory courses in mathematics, chemistry and physical chemistry are offered prior to the start of the Master's programme.

As a participant in the MBA programme at EBS, you will experience an ideal integration of theory and practice. The study programme provides you with state-of-the-art management know-how and economic expertise at a high academic level. This is supported by regular exchanges with companies through excursions, case studies, expert workshops, and guest lectures.
The MBA programme offers a well-balanced mix of different study modules that prepare you both professionally and personally for a leadership position.
• Global skills, local insights
• Unveiling the numbers
• Leading with influence
• Navigating the financial landscape
• Mastering business projects and processes
• The innovator’s toolkit (incl. a stay at SRH Haarlem University in the Netherlands)
• Sustainable operations

programmes.courseOrganisation:
A unique start to your studies.
Jump straight in at the deep end with the Social Impact Challenge during the MBA Onboarding Week. You will work on a real-life case study for a local company with your fellow students. At the end of the week, you compete as a team and present your work.
One study programme, two options
MBA, full-time: The study programme provides you with in-depth knowledge of economics, management know-how, and intercultural skills, as well as supporting your personal development. It thus optimally prepares you for a management position. The MBA is designed as a full-time programme over two semesters and offers you an efficient way to achieve your career goals.
MBA, part-time: Complete your MBA programme at EBS with maximum flexibility – without any loss of salary. With this version of the EBS MBA, you have the opportunity to extend your studies to four semesters. This allows you to combine the advantages of part-time study with the full study experience of a classic full-time programme.
programmes.internships: As full-time MBA students, you may choose to complete an internship of at least four weeks in a field related to your programme of study. The aim of the internship is to enable you to apply your academic knowledge in a business environment. The internship will be assessed through a project paper that focuses on the link between theory and practice.

We are happy to help you find affordable, furnished, and convenient accommodation near the campus. To make this process as efficient as possible for you, we provide an online accommodation/apartment forum on our student platform. There, you will find all vacant, private apartments near EBS Universität. You have automatic access once you have enrolled to study at EBS. Learn more about life at EBS...

programmes.description:
What is the MBA&E in Life Science Management Programme?
The internationally accredited MBA & Engineering programme in Life Science Management bridges the gap between science and business. It is designed for professionals who want to combine expertise in life sciences with strong management skills.
You will gain
• industry-specific knowledge in the international life sciences sector
• practical management expertise taught by industry professionals
• advanced management skills for the global Biotech, Biopharma, Medtech and Digital Health sector.
Who is this programme for?
This purely English-taught postgraduate degree is ideal for
• natural scientists
• business professionals
• engineers.
The programme helps you to
• apply your academic background to real-world life science challenges
• develop leadership and decision-making skills
• create your individual international life science network
• expand your management expertise with industry-focused knowledge
• gain international work experience.
What career opportunities can you expect?
After graduation, you will be prepared to
• take on managerial roles in the life science industry
• make strategic business decisions
• work in international and interdisciplinary environments.
Over 96% of graduates are employed within three months.
Which companies hire Life Science Management graduates?
Graduates of the MBA & Engineering in Life Science Management programme work across the global life sciences industry – from innovative start-ups to leading multinational companies.
Examples of employers include Bayer, Pfizer, Biotronik, Capgemini, IGES Institute, TissUse, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Otsuka Pharma and FyoniBio.
These roles span consulting, biotech, pharmaceuticals, and healthcare innovation.
Why study in Berlin?
Berlin is one of Europe’s leading Life Science Hubs. You benefit from
• a strong ecosystem in:
• Biotechnology
• Medical engineering
• Pharmaceuticals
• close collaboration with:
• Research institutes
• Innovative companies
• Public institutions.
Check out our LSM Flyer.

programmes.description:
At the NIT Northern Institute of Technology Management, you can study Technology Management in an individualised manner.
Depending on your personal goals, you can complete your studies at the NIT with a Master's degree or a double degree in combination with a Master's degree in engineering or natural sciences at the TUHH Hamburg University of Technology.
Over 25 years of experience in technology management
For more than 25 years, the NIT has attracted outstanding students and lecturers from all over the world. They benefit from an international and intercultural atmosphere in which ideas are openly discussed and innovative projects are put into practice.
Management studies at the NIT have always offered a strong practical orientation that is promoted by a constant exchange with partners from business and science.
LEARN MORE ABOUT OUR MASTER'S DEGREE PROGRAMME IN TECHNOLOGY MANAGEMENT
Ideal conditions in an agile, digital working environment
The Master's programme in Technology Management combines technical and scientific knowledge with management methods and entrepreneurship. Thanks to the special learning concept at the NIT, students learn in a practice-oriented way, independently and in teams. They expand their skills, learn about the latest innovation methods and train their entrepreneurial thinking.
DISCOVER OUR INNOVATIVE CURRICULUM
SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAMMES
Particularly outstanding applicants can apply for a scholarship. Some of the NIT’s partner companies offer industrial scholarships and, after an intensive selection process, pay the tuition fees for students studying at the NIT. Renowned partner companies of the NIT like Procter & Gamble, NXP, or IBM offer industrial scholarships for students studying toward a double Master's degree. We also offer own fellowship programmes like the NIT innovation scholarship for students with an innovative mindset, a high degree of social responsibility and a track record of high academic achievement.
FINANCING & SCHOLARSHIPS OPTIONS

programmes.internships:

If students carry out their projects in cooperation with companies, they can test direct applications on site during the practical phase lasting several weeks, test their product or service in direct contact with customers and get to know other relevant relationships in the company and on the corresponding market.
The internship experience also serves personal career orientation. Students get to know industries and companies/start-ups with relevance for their future career paths. Application Process
The required documents include:

Acceptance and Confirmation
Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis throughout the academic year. Candidates will generally be given notification on the status of their application within two weeks. Once accepted, students have one month to confirm their places.
Kindly complete the online application, upload all required documents and send it to us online.
We have a three-step admissions process:
• After uploading the required documents for evaluation to www.uni-assist.de, the first step is to submit an online application, which includes assembling a variety of materials that will help us assess your qualifications.
• Thereupon you are invited to participate in an initial selection interview. It typically takes 15 minutes and is designed to evaluate your suitability, motivation and qualification.
• Finally, after the completion of steps one and two, the programme director may invite you to a final interview.

programmes.description:
Unlock your finance career with Coburg University’s specialised MBA in Financial Management. Located in Bavaria, Germany, this two‑year, 120 ECTS, fully English‑taught, full‑time programme is designed for ambitious professionals aiming to combine management expertise with advanced financial skills in an international setting.
Our MBA brings together experienced students from over 80 countries, creating a vibrant, cross‑cultural learning atmosphere from which both international and German students benefit. The programme prepares graduates for senior leadership roles and ultimately for a CFO career path.
Why choose Coburg?
• CFO‑level skills: Build expertise across corporate finance, financial markets, treasury and risk management, financial accounting, etc.
• Real‑world experience: Hands‑on projects and a 20‑week internship with top German companies; many students receive job offers before graduation.
• State‑of‑the‑art resources: Access to our Bloomberg Lab and cutting‑edge financial data tools, Bloomberg Certification
• Global outlook: Study entirely in English alongside a diverse cohort and expand your network in Germany’s financial sector.
• Top accreditation: FIBAA premium seal; accredited by the German Accreditation Council through 2030
• Career success: 85% of graduates remain in Germany to build their careers.
Optional dual degrees with UniSC (Australia) or MRIIRS (India) are available without extending study time.
Target Group
Young professionals with proven intellectual capability and strong leadership potential
What makes our MBA unique?
• Specialised MBA with a highly international student group
• Integration into the German job market via a 20-week internship
• Excellent learning environment (1:6 instructor/student ratio)
• Syllabus inclusion of an A2 German language certificate
• Bloomberg Lab and Certification
• Competitive tuition fees and extraordinary services and support
• MBA programme with the FIBAA premium seal
• Our elective courses help build your expertise for specific career goals.
For more information, please consult our website or take a look at our brochure.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The MBA Financial Management programme is divided into four semesters and consists of five pillars:
• Base modules in general management and core modules in financial management
• A selection of elective modules on current topics
• German Intensive Courses I and II
• Application & transfer modules
• Master’s thesis or Capstone Project
Six base modules cover mainstream topics of general management (e.g. Financial and Management Accounting).
Five core modules form the specialisation in financial management (e.g. International Economics).
Electives enable students to develop expertise aligned with their career ambitions. Students choose four modules, including:
• AI Applications in Finance
• Applied Risk Management
• Code and Capital (with Python)
• Crypto Currencies and Blockchain
• Current Topics in International Finance
• Digital Transformation & Innovative Finance
• Econometrics
• European History and Culture
• Financial Derivatives
• Financial Statistics
• Financial Planning and Analysis
• Introduction to Islamic Finance & Banking
• Investment Valuation (Bloomberg Applications)
• Issues in Political Science
• Mergers and Acquisitions
• Operations Management
• Quantitative Methods in Finance
• Risk and Insurance Management
• SAP-FI
• Sustainable Finance
Core and base modules are credited with five ECTS. Electives are credited with three ECTS.
Languages and Internship
During the first two semesters, international students attend German language courses, enabling confident communication after one year. German native speakers may choose other foreign languages instead.
In the third semester, students complete a five-month internship at an index-listed company in Europe/Germany (member of Euro Stoxx, DAX30, M-DAX, S-DAX or TecDAX).
The application and transfer courses are Management of Projects and Business Simulation; Project Placement & Coaching. These courses ensure a smooth transition between theory and practice, and they are enhanced by the internship, field trips, and academic excursions.
Having successfully participated in the requisite modules, you will be able to focus on your Master's thesis or Capstone Project (Master’s thesis alternative) in the fourth semester (four months). Many students choose to conduct research on an innovative theme in one of their courses, while others prefer a topic relating to their internship tasks or the practical challenges faced by a company.
programmes.internships:
An internship at a German company (no work permit required) is an integral part of the study programme and is scheduled for the third semester. During the internship, students have the opportunity to apply the theoretical knowledge and skills obtained in the programme as well as to become familiar with German business customs. The internship lasts 20 weeks. German students who have never studied or worked abroad are encouraged to do the internship abroad.
The programme has developed a large internship database, and substantial contact data will be provided upon request.
Internship Workshop
As part of our programme, each year we invite top companies such as BMW, Adidas and EY, along with leading banks, healthcare and insurance companies to give students the opportunity to complete their dream internship and gain insight into their internship opportunities. Students will learn how to craft their resumes and cover letters to highlight the specific skills and experience sought by the various companies. The workshop offers students the opportunity to connect with former employees of various financial services companies and gain mentorship.
By combining practical skills development with real industry knowledge, this workshop empowers our students to move confidently through their application process.
Additional highlights include company visits and a multi‑day academic excursion to a European financial centre, strengthening networking skills and employer connections.
programmes.partTimeJobs:
There are job opportunities in the city of Coburg. However, please be aware that this is a full-time programme and that the schedule is structured accordingly.
The integrated internship in the third semester is usually financially compensated.
Students who exhibit competitive academic performance may serve as tutors/teaching assistants in our programme.

You can find more information about the student residences in Coburg on the website of "Studentenwerk Oberfranken".
For information on private housing, see: http://www.studenten-wg.de.

• Competence to apply cross-cultural management skills in negotiations, marketing, leadership etc., in order to examine and evaluate the complexity of culture within organisations

• Ability to outline energy-consuming activities and potential sources of emissions from transport, identify measures, assess sustainability and suggest responsible logistics, and compose strategies for the sustainable development of supply chains
• Knowledge of international business law and the practice of the conclusion of contracts and conflict resolution in international commerce; insight into the tax systems and in-depth knowledge about taxes most relevant to enterprises involved in international business; ability to assess tax-related advantages and disadvantages of different legal forms, corporate strategies and location factors

programmes.description:
The MBA distance learning programme in Innovation Management programme is designed for professionals aiming to drive change and growth in their organisations through systematic innovation strategies. It combines theoretical knowledge with practical methods and tools to empower students to successfully lead innovation processes and develop new business models.
Key focus areas include:
• General Management and Business Fundamentals
• Innovation Management in Companies: process design, business model innovation, open innovation approaches, frugal innovation, and intellectual property management
• Building an Innovation-Oriented Culture: leadership skills, creativity methods, organisational design (New Work), and values-based innovation
• Systematic Innovation Methods: TRIZ, design thinking, trend analysis, and other methods for structured idea generation and problem-solving
• Digitalisation and Sustainability: integration of digital transformation and sustainable practices as essential drivers of innovation
• Case studies and real-world insights: analysis of successful innovative companies and participation in international conferences such as the ISPIM Innovation Conference
This MBA course of study enables students to develop a deep understanding of the role of innovation as a core competitive advantage, equipping them to shape and implement successful innovation strategies across diverse industries.
Students can take advantage of intensive support and develop their know-how in the environment of a cooperative working atmosphere.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The programme is divided into four semesters:
• Semesters 1 & 2: Business fundamentals, including management frameworks, financial and quantitative methods, marketing, communication, and leadership
• Semester 3: Specialised modules on innovation management, leadership in innovation-friendly cultures, and systematic innovation methods
• Semester 4: Master’s thesis, accompanied by participation in an international seminar and presentation of research outcomes
The structure and teaching methods follow a hybrid and blended learning approach, combining self-study, online/face-to-face teaching on three to four weekends per semester. In small groups, the learning content can be deepened.
• Self-directed study with comprehensive learning materials (learning letters) designed for independent and flexible learning
• Online courses and digital learning platforms, allowing students to study from anywhere and at their own pace
• Intensive use of applied teaching methods such as simulations, group projects, and presentations to prepare students for real-world challenges
• The types of assessment are written examinations, seminar papers, project presentations, Master's thesis, and colloquium.
This structure is specifically designed to allow students to continue working alongside their studies, offering maximum flexibility and practice-oriented learning.
You will be supported by a team of professors with practical experience and numerous company contacts, as well as executives and experts in specialist lectures.
With this and the contact to fellow students, you will build up an excellent network. Use this opportunity as a booster for your professional networking and development!

programmes.description:
MBA in Leadership & Supply Chain Management
The MBA follows a coherent learning journey designed to support confident and consistent professional growth. It begins with Management Essentials, a foundation covering core disciplines such as strategy and competitive positioning, financial decision-making, customer and market management, and operations and supply chain fundamentals. This phase strengthens analytical thinking across functions, develops a shared management language, and builds a holistic understanding of how organisations create value in international settings.
Building on this foundation, the programme moves into the Transformational Leadership Programme, shifting the focus from managing systems to leading people, organisations, and change. Participants strengthen their leadership capabilities in areas such as change management, ethics and responsible leadership, diversity and inclusion, conflict resolution, and leading teams in international environments.
In parallel, participants deepen their expertise through one of two complementary specialisations: Digital Operations, focusing on intelligent automation, foundations of AI and machine learning, process mining, data strategy, and risk sensing and scenario planning; or Organisational Resilience, focusing on circular supply chains, sustainability hotspots, ESG regulation and compliance, and responsible sourcing.
A central element of the programme is the Impact Project, a real business challenge from the participant's own organisation that runs throughout the MBA, translating classroom insights directly into professional practice. Two integrated international study trips — to destinations such as Universidad de los Andes in Colombia and KLU's campus in Vietnam — provide first-hand exposure to global trade dynamics and emerging markets. The programme concludes with a Master thesis, in which participants apply their acquired knowledge to a specific topic of their choice.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
Course Organisation
The part-time MBA runs over 18 months in a monthly block-seminar format: participants attend intensive four-day sessions (Friday to Monday) on KLU's Hamburg campus, allowing them to study alongside their full-time role. The curriculum follows four consecutive phases:
• Phase 1 – Management Essentials: Core disciplines such as strategy and competitive positioning, financial decision-making, customer and market management, and operations and supply chain fundamentals.
• Phase 2 – Transformational Leadership Programme: A shift from managing systems to leading people, organisations, and change, covering topics such as change management, ethics and responsible leadership, diversity and inclusion, and conflict resolution.
• Phase 3 – Specialisation: Participants choose one of two paths — Digital Operations or Organisational Resilience — and deepen their expertise through targeted modules, practical applications, and two integrated international study trips to destinations such as Colombia and Vietnam.
• Phase 4 – Master's Thesis: Participants dive deep into a specific topic of their choice, supported by faculty guidance, applying everything they've learned throughout the programme.

programmes.courseOrganisation:
Participants in the International Business Management & Leadership MBA programme have a variety of scheduling options to individually customise the MBA programme. One option for international students is to study our programme in the Fast Track version for 18 months, including the Master's thesis. You start in September. You are able to do this on a full-time basis, but it is also possible to do this while you work.
The other option is to study on a part-time basis for five semesters in the Standard Track variation.
The format of this programme is blended learning (mix of face-to-face seminars, online self-study phase/web-based learning and live web sessions or coaching according to defined learning objectives).
You will join different MBA groups for the seminars. Since most classes are offered at least twice per year, MBA participants can also set up an individual schedule and a mixture between blended learning and online flex studies. Most classes are at the weekend or online in the evening hours.
During the week, you will work on your assignments or participate in web-based learning, online live classes, coaching or German classes. Should you not be able to attend certain seminars for professional, family or personal reasons, these courses can be taken with one of our parallel MBA groups or retaken during a subsequent semester.

programmes.description:
Your stepping stone for a management career in international companies!
Our Master's programme in "International Business with Regional Focus“ is the perfect starting point for those who want to take on management positions in the global world of business. You will learn all that you need to know as a manager in international companies. In every course, the programme is thus characterised by a high practice orientation and a focus on the specifics of doing business in an international setting. After one and a half years of studies in Würzburg, the prestigious MBA degree (Master of Business Administration) is awarded to you.
Programme Structure
The lectures take place in Würzburg and mainly on Fridays and Saturdays.
The first semester takes place from early October to end of January for all students in Würzburg.
At the beginning of the second semester (around March), students that have chosen the focus regions Asia or Latin America will stay at a partner university in Taiwan or Colombia for about three weeks, where Module 5 is taught to them. Students who have chosen the focus region Europe will be taught Module 5 in Würzburg. The remainder of the second semester (till the end of July) takes place in Würzburg for all students.
The third semester starts again in early October and takes place in Würzburg for all students. The Master's thesis can be written at THWS, at the partner university abroad or with a company.
Programme Contents
The first semester focuses on the following aspects:
• Harmonising the knowledge base of the students
• Acquaintance or deepening of language and intercultural skills as the basis for acquiring knowledge about the chosen focus region
• Acquiring methodical skills in project management and research projects, specifically as the basis for project work and the Master's thesis
The second semester focuses on the following aspects:
• Acquiring knowledge about the chosen focus region
• Acquiring professional skills
The third semester focuses on the following aspects:
• Acquiring further professional skills
• Finishing the programme with the individual Master's thesis
programmes.courseOrganisation:

• Module 1: Business Decisions (Courses: Decision Theory and Practice, Innovation Management and Entrepreneurship)
• Module 2: Language Competence Europe / Asia / Latin America (Courses: General Language Competence German / Mandarin / Spanish, Business Language Competence German / Mandarin / Spanish)
• Module 3: Intercultural Management (Courses: Organisational Behaviour, Cross Cultural Management)
• Module 4: Project Management (Courses: Research Projects, International Project Management)
In the second semester, the following modules and courses are taught:
• Module 5: Doing Business In and With Western Europe / Asia / Latin America
• Module 6: Managing International Businesses (Courses: International Management, International Economics)
• Module 7: Strategic Competences (Courses: Strategic Management, Operations Strategy in the Digital Age)
• Module 8: International Financial Management (Courses: International Management Control, International Finance)
• Module 9: International Leadership (Courses: Organisational Development and Leadership, Business Ethics)
• Module 10: Managing International Markets (Courses: International Marketing, Management of International Supply Chains)
In the third semester, the following modules and courses are taught:
• Module 11: International Regulatory Frameworks (Courses: International Law, International Financial Reporting)
• Module 12: Information Technology (Courses: Management Information Systems, Business Game)
• Module 13: Master's Thesis

programmes.description:
The MBA Motorsport Management is a unique distance learning programme designed to provide professionals with advanced knowledge and practical skills in management within the motorsport industry. Participants gain in-depth insights into the structures and processes of international motorsport, covering topics from team and event management to motorsport marketing and logistics.
Key areas of study include:
• General Management and Business Fundamentals: business administration, finance, economics, quantitative methods, and strategic marketing to build a strong managerial foundation
• Motorsport Organisation and Governance: structures and regulations in motorsport series, team and personnel management, logistics, and track and event operations
• Motorsport Marketing and Sponsorship: motorsport-specific marketing strategies, sponsorship and financing, public relations, social media, and brand management
• Legal and Regulatory Aspects: understanding the legal frameworks and compliance requirements that shape the global motorsport environment
• Practical Motorsport Management Skills: hands-on insights into event planning, team leadership, and operational management through case studies and real-world projects
• International Networking and Exposure: participation in international seminars and conferences, such as the FIA Sport Conference, providing valuable industry connections and global perspectives
The programme is delivered via a blended learning approach, combining self-study materials, online modules, and an interactive seminar at the FIA conference. This format enables students to integrate studies with their professional careers.
Students can take advantage of intensive support and develop their know-how in the environment of a cooperative working atmosphere.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The MBA Motorsport Management is structured into four semesters. The first year covers fundamental business administration and management modules, including communication and leadership skills. The second year focuses on motorsport-specific subjects such as organisation and marketing, followed by the Master's thesis.
A detailed overview:
• Semesters 1 & 2: General management modules (economics, quantitative analysis, financial management, and strategic marketing)
• Semester 3: Organisation and governance in motorsport, personnel and project management, motorsport logistics, event and track management, Sponsorship, social media, public relations, brand and innovation management, legal frameworks
• Semester 4: Students complete a Master's thesis and attend international conferences such as the FIA Sport Conference to enhance their global network and practical exposure
The structure and teaching methods follow a hybrid and blended learning approach, combining self-study, online/face-to-face teaching on three to four weekends per semester. In small groups, the learning content can be deepened.
• Self-directed study with comprehensive learning materials (learning letters) designed for independent and flexible learning
• Online courses and digital learning platforms, allowing students to study from anywhere and at their own pace
• Intensive use of applied teaching methods such as simulations, group projects, and presentations to prepare students for real-world challenges
• The types of assessment are written examinations, seminar papers, project presentations, Master's thesis and colloquium.
This structure is specifically designed for working professionals, providing maximum flexibility while ensuring a high degree of practical relevance and direct application to the motorsport industry.
You will be supported by a team of professors with practical experience and numerous company contacts, as well as executives and experts in specialist lectures.
With this and the contact to fellow students, you will build up an excellent network. Use this opportunity as a booster for your professional networking and development!

programmes.description:
MPE places emphasis on engineering fundamentals so that you can seamlessly combine the previous knowledge you have acquired at the universities where you completed your Bachelor's degree with German engineering thinking. With our special "TRAINING IN ..." courses, we want to ensure that you speak the same technical language as your colleagues trained in Germany, building on which there are further practical and application-oriented in-depth engineering subjects.
Another important part of the degree programme consists of modules in which you will be familiarised with the state-of-the-art simulation tools used in mechanical engineering and process engineering. The degree programme includes modules on flow simulation (CFD), strength calculation (DEM) and process simulation. Here you will be trained both theoretically and in practical exercises. The programme as a whole also focuses on project-based learning, in which you can apply your skills in small projects, mainly as group work, from the second semester onwards. As a small university, we offer very good support here. In project work, you will always have a contact person who will guide you through the project. Of course, we also expect you to work independently and in an engineering environment, as you are studying for a Master's degree.
In today's world, business skills and knowledge are also important for engineers. This is why we offer a wide range of modules from the field of economics, particularly in the area of electives, which teach you skills in the field of industrial engineering.
The process engineering content accompanies the mechanical engineering content throughout the four semesters of the degree programme. As a resource university, we have placed the focus here on secondary raw materials/recycling. We will continue to expand this in the coming years so that you can acquire comprehensive knowledge in the field of recycling technologies as part of the degree programme. Together with the competences from the field of mechanical engineering (conception and construction), you will also be able to develop and evaluate a design for recycling.
You will be involved in research as part of your final thesis (Master's thesis) and will be able to apply the knowledge you have learnt to practical projects and contribute to a scientific solution to an engineering problem. In this context, it is important to us that we can integrate you into our application-oriented research during your Master's thesis at the latest.
TU Bergakademie Freiberg will enable you to take German courses that build on each other for the entire duration of your studies.
Job opportunities: mechanical industry, e.g. automotive industry, manufacturing, plant engineering or processing; scientific sector: universities, research institutions
programmes.courseOrganisation:
• In the first semester, courses in Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer, Fluid Dynamics, Particle Technology, Process Equipment, Endurance and Design are compulsory to ensure that all of the students in the programme have the same academic background.
• The second semester provides the theoretical framework. To develop self-reliant scientific working techniques, students are required to work on projects in small teams. Students gain additional knowledge and experience by interacting with university scientists and engineers.
• In the third semester, students become familiar with design methods and learn at least one numerical tool.
• In addition, basic courses in management, economy and finance are offered as electives.
• During the fourth semester, students will finally work on their research-oriented Master's theses, which must be presented and defended.
Methods of teaching can be lectures, workshops, seminars, practicals and other types of courses. Seminars lead the students to independent scientific work through discussions and presentations. Besides the consolidation of theoretical knowledge, the aim of practicals is to allow students to learn methods and other practical skills.

programmes.description:
The Bachelor's degree programme in Mechanical Engineering offers a thorough engineering education focusing on design and manufacturing of machines and systems. By studying mainly interdisciplinary courses, students acquire the ability and competence to solve complex engineering problems. Next to this solid basic education in mechanical engineering, students are taught the modelling of mathematical and physical processes, plus their computer-aided analysis. This enables students to gain a comprehensive understanding of technical systems and to develop innovative solutions.
In the first semesters, students acquire essential knowledge in mathematics, mechanics, natural sciences and technical representation, all of which is required to soundly comprehend technical systems and develop practical solutions and applications for them.
In further modules, topics such as thermodynamics, materials science, electrical engineering and information technology are covered in greater depth. Systemic and analytical thinking is being encouraged by all teaching staff, a skill that is indispensable for engineering issues and topics.
The Bachelor's degree provides entry either into a Master's degree programme or directly into the professional world of technology. The expertise and key skills acquired during the programme form the basis for a successful career in mechanical engineering and add to shaping the technologies of tomorrow.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The first two semesters offer general orientation, both in the subject matter and the German culture and language. Hence, in the first year, the language of instruction in this Bachelor’s degree programme for the basic subjects is English. In addition, language courses are offered. The remaining four semesters are taught in German and English, and they further the knowledge expected to successfully finish with a degree.
In addition to the compulsory courses in the curriculum, you will have the opportunity to pursue personal engineering interests in elective courses. Methods of teaching include practical laboratory assignments and participation in project team work. Non-technical courses are also integrated into the curriculum which serve to develop soft skills and key qualifications.
The degree programme concludes with the Bachelor’s thesis. The thesis illustrates your ability to work independently and within a given time frame on a specific problem from the field of Engineering using scientific method. Bachelor graduates are qualified to continue their studies in a postgraduate (so-called consecutive) or interdisciplinary Master’s programme. However, you can also use your Bachelor’s degree to enter the job market directly.

programmes.description:
Mechanical and plant engineering is one of the largest and most future-proof high-tech sectors in Germany. By combining mechanical engineering with electrical engineering, measurement, control engineering and information technology, new products and processes are constantly being developed. The Master's degree programme in Mechanical Engineering is divided into seven specialisations.
The General Mechanical Engineering specialisation offers a broad, traditional education in mechanical engineering. Besides the sound technical basis, the curriculum includes elective options that allow students to design their own profiles.
The Mechatronics specialisation combines traditional mechanical engineering with electrical engineering and information technology. Students learn the basics of developing and manufacturing mechatronic systems in which mechanical, electrical and electronic components are integrated in innovative modules.
Global markets and value chains require new and efficient material flows. In the Production and Logistics specialisation, students acquire methods for planning, developing and controlling production and logistics processes in supply chains. The programme combines technical aspects with organisational and economic requirements and prepares students for interdisciplinary activities.
In view of the global climate problem and scarcity of resources, energy and environmental technology plays a key role. This specialisation qualifies students for the development of resource-saving systems and technologies to reduce environmental pollution in soil, water and air.
Maritime systems are among the most complex large-scale structures and facilities built by humans. On the one hand, these systems contain a high degree of specific, closely interlinked, complex subsystems and need to be operated with a high degree of efficiency, but on the other hand, they have to cope with the harsh environmental conditions at sea. The Sustainable and Autonomous Maritime Systems specialisation addresses the need for highly qualified engineers. The foundation of general mechanical engineering is enhanced by industry-specific knowledge in the field of ship and offshore technology.
The Maritime Systems Safety specialisation addresses issues relating to the safety of maritime systems. Specific content of safety-relevant areas of ship and offshore technology as well as knowledge of risk assessment, functional safety, diagnosis of systems, system reliability, and process control technology are taught.
The Turbomachinery specialisation focuses on the physical relationships of energy conversion in the form of shaft power, e.g. for power generation and the conveyance of media. In addition to product development, this includes the thermodynamic, aerodynamic and rotor-dynamic design of turbomachinery with the aid of current development and research tools.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
All Master's degree programmes follow the same structure and consist of core subjects, advanced theories, profile subjects, elective courses and the Master's thesis. The mandatory core subjects are obligatory for all students and provide in-depth knowledge in the specific discipline. The subjects of a profile specialise in a specific area within this discipline. The elective courses can be chosen out of any discipline in engineering. The overall language of instruction for each Master's degree programme is 50% English and 50% German.
In both industry and universities, there is a worldwide and long-term need for engineering graduates. The ISE programme corresponds to global market conditions and was designed to match the job requirements for graduates. It particularly offers subjects of specific international relevance. Apart from the technical qualification, the linguistic and cultural aspects offer special advantages for graduates in a global job market and qualify them for responsible positions in international companies or for a continuation of their academic career, e.g. when heading for a PhD.

programmes.description:
The innovative Mechanical Engineering (BEng) study programme offers a comprehensive education in fields such as computer-aided product design (CAD), computer-aided engineering (CAE), production automation, robotics, IT, and AI.
Students can choose from five distinct specialisation branches:
• Product Development and Lightweight Construction
• Pharmaceutical Engineering
• Food Engineering
• Mechatronics and Autonomous Systems
• General Mechanical Engineering
The programme spans seven semesters and equips students with a versatile skill set.
Our degree in Mechanical Engineering offers diverse career opportunities across various sectors — ranging from Automotive, Aerospace, and Energy Supply to Machine Tools, Plant Engineering, Defence, and Pharmaceuticals.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The course is divided into three main parts:
• Basic studies in Mechanical Engineering (four semesters)
• Fundamentals in mathematics, mechanics, materials science, thermodynamics, computer technologies/programming
• Electric and electronic technology, electric drives and generators, measurement technology, control technology
• Manufacturing of products, machine tools, automation, economics
• Product design, CAD and design elements
• Internship in engineering position (one semester) in a company
• Branches of studies (two semesters)
• Product Development and Light Weight Construction
• Design methodology, finite element simulation, advanced mechanics, machine dynamics, motion technology, light weight materials, light weight methodology, strength of materials
• Mechatronics and Autonomous Systems
• Motion technology, machine dynamics, virtual and augmented reality/digital plant, artificial intelligence, machine vision, practise in control technology, image analysis
• Pharmaceutical Engineering
• Forms of pharmaceutical, planning and systematics of pharmaceutical processes, machine design for pharmaceutical industry, packaging technology, sterile design of machines, regulations and legal aspects in design of pharmaceutical machines and production processes, quality management in pharmaceutical industry
• Food Engineering
• Food science, planning and systematics of food production processes, machine design for food and beverage industry, packaging technology, sterile design of machines, hygiene and clean-room-technology, regulations and legal aspects in design of food production machines and production processes, quality management in food and beverage industry
• General Mechanical Engineering
• Wide range of different innovative topics

programmes.description:
The Mechanical Engineering Bachelor’s programme provides you with a solid foundation in all major areas of mechanical engineering – including mechanics, thermodynamics, materials science and production engineering. On top of that, you’ll gain specialised knowledge in product and technology development as well as simulation techniques using modern software tools.
From the very beginning, practical projects and hands-on lab work are part of the curriculum, helping you connect theory with real-world challenges. You’ll learn how to model and simulate physical processes to make better design decisions and improve technical efficiency.
Teamwork, creativity and interdisciplinary thinking are at the heart of this programme. You’ll collaborate in small groups, work on innovative solutions, and regularly present your ideas to experts – just like in a real engineering job.
Graduates are well-prepared for a wide range of careers in dynamic industries such as automotive, aerospace, mechanical systems, and R&D. Whether you become a development engineer, simulation specialist or project manager – this degree opens up excellent opportunities in Germany and beyond.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
Starting the first semester with virtual / online teaching
We do not expect any special prior knowledge at the start of the course, just a basic knowledge of mathematics and science at school level and a command of English (level B2) – no German. In this first semester, you will cross the bridge from school to the University of Applied Sciences!
• Mathematics and Scientific Basics
• Soft Skills and Culture
• English and German (level A2)
First study section (basics): semester two and three
The foundation modules in the second and third semesters are:
• Technical Mathematics
• Mechanics
• Engineering Design and Machine Elements
• Electrical Engineering
• Programming
• Material Science
• Business Administration
Second study phase (mechanical engineering specialisation): semester four, five and six
After mastering the engineering basics, the professional specialisation follows:
• Mathematical Applications
• Simulation Methods
• Advanced Mechanics (Strength of Materials, Dynamics)
• Engineering Design and Machine Elements
• Control Systems
• Measurement Technology
• Fluid Mechanics and Thermodynamics
• Advanced Material Science
• Production Technology
• Digitalisation in Production
• Scientific Work and Lab Workshops
• Elective Subjects
Internship and final semester including the Bachelor's thesis
The practical semester comprises 20 weeks of full-time work experience and two practical courses.
• Industrial internship
• Seminars accompanying the internship like Project Management
• Elective subject
• Engineering project (can be combined with the Bachelor's thesis)
• Bachelor's thesis and seminar
Module manual
In some modules, teaching takes place together with students from the fields of natural sciences and electrical engineering. You can make valuable contacts, look beyond the boundaries of mechanical engineering and benefit from the experience and skills of your fellow students. The insight into different approaches and procedures in problem solving will be very fruitful for your personal development. You will learn how to work effectively with specialists from other disciplines, which is often necessary in complex projects.

The industrial internship can be your first step towards a career in Germany.

programmes.description:
This degree programme prepares you to become a qualified specialist in the field of mechanical engineering.
The programme lasts three semesters and leads to a Master of Engineering (MEng). The course initially offers advanced modules in general mechanical engineering and modules in management and project management. You also have the opportunity to specialise in the areas of plant engineering, design or production engineering, by choosing from a catalogue of modules in these specialisations. In addition to the lectures, your studies also include a substantial project component. The Master's programme can be studied either entirely in English or in German, but you may also freely choose between English- and German-taught modules.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The Master's degree course in Mechanical Engineering is divided into three parts in the first two semesters. One part of the curriculum (10 CP) consists of two modules with 5 CP each, which are compulsory. Here you will learn leadership and project management skills as well as advanced technical fundamentals.
Part 1:
The compulsory modules are:
• Advanced Project Management for Engineers 5 CP
• Lightweight Construction and Innovative Materials 5 CP
Part 2:
You can specialise in the elective part of the programme. In particular, the specialisations from the Bachelor's degree course in Mechanical Engineering (Plant Engineering, Production Engineering, Design Engineering) and intersections thereof are considered here. You may choose freely from a catalogue, but you must take at least 30 CP (6 modules). For guidance, the modules are marked according to their main subject area (A = plant engineering, P = production engineering, K = design engineering).
Examples for elective modules (in English) are:
• Advanced Vehicle Dynamics
• Advanced ERP Systems
• Energy Process Simulation
• Project Wind Challenge
• Hyperloop Project
• Modular Systems and Module Management
• Advanced Thermodynamics
• Laser Material Processing
• Data Science / Software Development
• Simulation of Production Technology
• Advanced Control Theory
An overview of the modules can be found on the website and in the module handbook.
Part 3:
The third part of the first two semesters is the project area. Here you will learn how to conduct scientific work in technical projects. The aim is to prepare you for management and project management tasks in industry as well as for research work — for example, during a doctorate.
In the third semester, you will complete your Master's thesis, which you can typically carry out in a company or in one of our university's laboratories.

There is one fully-furnished student dormitory, called “Steinweg 20”. Residence halls in Emden are not managed by the University of Applied Sciences Emden/Leer. Rather, they are managed by an independent organisation, the "Studierendenwerk". Therefore, we are not in a position to guarantee an accommodation in such dorms. Please note that move-in times are restricted due to semester dates.
Find more information here: Studierendenwerk Oldenburg

Additionally, the International Office has various contacts for students who seek private accommodations.

programmes.description:
Master’s Programme in Mechanical Engineering
This Master’s degree programme prepares graduates for a wide range of professional roles in mechanical engineering. Students acquire a broad and up-to-date foundation in the field, with a particular emphasis on advanced applications of computer-aided technologies in engineering and manufacturing.
Throughout the programme, students deepen their expertise by choosing one of three specialisations:
• Engineering – focusing on development and design engineering
• Digitalisation – focusing on digital manufacturing and smart production
• Sustainability – focusing on sustainable solutions in mechanical engineering
Specialisation: Engineering
Students specialising in Engineering expand their knowledge in areas such as finite element methods, drive technology, control engineering, materials science, process and manufacturing informatics, and product data management. The programme strengthens multidisciplinary thinking as well as analytical and problem-solving skills required for complex engineering tasks.
Specialisation: Digitalisation
The Digitalisation specialisation provides in-depth knowledge in automation, process and manufacturing informatics, and product data management. Particular emphasis is placed on digital manufacturing, graphical simulation, and manufacturing simulation. Through project-based learning, students further develop their interdisciplinary, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.
Specialisation: Sustainability
Students choosing the Sustainability specialisation focus on the development and evaluation of sustainable design and production solutions. The curriculum addresses environmental, economic, and ethical aspects of sustainability, enabling students to assess the sustainability of mechanical engineering products and their manufacturing processes and to apply appropriate evaluation strategies of products in mechanical engineering and their production processes.
Building on the knowledge gained throughout the programme, graduates are equipped to engage in research, develop optimised engineering solutions, and successfully manage complex challenges in modern mechanical engineering.
The programme concludes with a Master’s thesis, which students complete within a period of six months.

programmes.description: The goal of the university programme is to provide students with a subject-specific education in academic, personal, and social terms. The Master’s programme builds upon the foundational knowledge and specialisations gained in a prior Bachelor’s programme, enabling students to acquire an in-depth academic education in mechanical engineering with a specialisation in Energy and Process Engineering. Students are actively involved in research throughout the programme. Furthermore, through elements such as the internship conducted alongside the programme and the Master’s thesis with colloquium, key competencies — including communication and teamwork skills, presentation and public speaking abilities, and project management—as well as the ability to utilise modern information technologies, are further developed. Within the specialisation modules, students are integrated into engineering research. Through the colloquium at the conclusion of the Master’s thesis, students consolidate their ability to present engineering projects at the Master’s level. The programme prepares students for career paths that require advanced qualifications as mechanical engineers. It aims to train both professionals in leadership roles within the development and research departments of commercial enterprises and the next generation of scientists, as it generally opens the door to pursuing a doctorate in engineering upon completion of the Master’s programme.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
First, second, and third semesters: postgraduate courses in Advanced Fluid Dynamics, Advanced Thermodynamics, and Signal Processing with the corresponding laboratories, as well as more than 18 elective modules are available so that each student can individually enhance their skills and knowledge.
Fourth semester: Master's thesis in one of the active research groups of the department.
Grades and credit points are based on the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS).
programmes.internships: An internship of six weeks is included in the programme. The internship may be replaced by a course module.
programmes.partTimeJobs: Students can find part-time jobs with the help of the job placement service of the university. Siegen and the surrounding area are home to a large number of medium-sized industrial enterprises (SMEs), or so-called hidden champions in electrical and mechanical engineering. Some bigger examples include the companies SMS and Achenbach Buschhütten. A lot of smaller, yet very successful and quickly growing high-tech companies are located here as well, for instance, PMD Technologies and Asentics, which are spin-off companies of the university. Therefore, there are employment prospects in the region, particularly for positions that are available during the semester break and following graduation.
programmes.accommodation:
There are student residences (dormitories) of the "Studierendenwerk" (student services) close to the university. The rent for a room is between 240 EUR and 460 EUR. Please be aware that German universities do not usually have campus systems like universities in some other countries, where all students can find accommodation directly on the university property. Therefore, some students might have to find rooms on their own. The private accommodation costs per room are 400 EUR on average. Detailed information concerning general accommodation can be found here.
Early application/search is advisable.

programmes.description: The goal of the university programme is to provide students with a subject-specific education in academic, personal, and social terms. The Master’s programme builds upon the foundational knowledge and specialisations gained in a prior Bachelor’s programme, enabling students to acquire an in-depth academic education in mechanical engineering with a specialisation in materials science. Students are actively involved in research throughout the programme. In addition, through elements such as the internship conducted alongside the programme and the Master’s thesis with colloquium, key competencies – including communication and teamwork skills, presentation and public speaking abilities, and project management – as well as the ability to utilise modern information technologies, are further developed. Within the specialisation modules, students are integrated into engineering research. Through the colloquium at the conclusion of the Master’s thesis, students consolidate their ability to present engineering projects at the Master’s level. The programme prepares students for career paths that require advanced qualifications as mechanical engineers. It aims to train both professionals in leadership roles within the development and research departments of commercial enterprises and the next generation of scientists, as it generally opens the door to pursuing a doctorate in engineering upon completion of the Master’s programme.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
First, second, and third semesters: postgraduate courses in Linear Theory of Elasticity, Advanced Thermodynamics, and Reliability of Technical Systems with the corresponding laboratories, as well as more than 18 elective modules are available so that each student can individually enhance their skills and knowledge.
Fourth semester: Master's thesis in one of the active research groups of the department.
Grades and credit points are based on the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS).
programmes.internships: An internship of six weeks is included in the programme. The internship may be replaced by a course module.
programmes.partTimeJobs: Students can find part-time jobs with the help of the job placement service of the university. Siegen and the surrounding area are home to a large number of medium-sized industrial enterprises (SMEs), or so-called hidden champions in electrical and mechanical engineering. Some bigger examples include the companies SMS and Achenbach Buschhütten. A lot of smaller, yet very successful and quickly growing high-tech companies are located here as well, for instance, PMD Technologies and Asentics, which are spin-off companies of the university. Therefore, there are employment prospects in the region, particularly for positions that are available during the semester break and following graduation.

Therefore, some students might have to find rooms on their own. The private accommodation costs per room are 400 EUR on average. programmes.description:
Studying the Master's in Mechanical Engineering provides significant advantages, including access to cutting-edge research facilities and strong industry connections. The programme emphasises practical, hands-on learning, ensuring students gain both theoretical knowledge and the skills needed to excel in today’s competitive marketplace.
Students can specialise in one of three fields or opt for a comprehensive general track:
• Mechanical Design and Development: This specialisation focuses on advanced design principles using sophisticated tools like finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to create innovative and sustainable engineering solutions.
• Energy and Process Engineering: Concentrates on thermodynamics, heat transfer, and fluid mechanics, emphasising efficient energy conversion systems. The curriculum includes renewable energy technologies and process optimisation to address global energy needs.
• Production Engineering: Covers essential manufacturing processes and technologies, focusing on manufacturing systems, automation, and circularity topics. Students learn to integrate circular economy principles, optimising resource use and reducing waste.
The general engineering track offers balanced coursework across core disciplines, providing flexibility for a range of career paths.
For more details on specialisation options and the programme structure, please visit the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering’s website:
https://www.maschinenbau.uni-hannover.de/studium/studiengaenge/maststudiengaenge/mechanical-engineering-english-track
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The English Track in the Master's programme in Mechanical Engineering is based on mandatory focus modules that cover key areas of each of the three specialisations "Mechanical Design and Development", "Energy and Process Engineering", and "Production Engineering".
Students can opt for a specialisation by selecting compulsory and elective subjects that match their interests and career goals. The programme also includes a student research project, offering hands-on experience in tackling real mechanical engineering challenges. A pivotal component is an industrial internship lasting at least 12 weeks, where students apply their theoretical knowledge in practical settings, crucial for their career development in preparation for the job market.
For international students, a German language course is mandatory to equip them with basic language skills necessary for daily and professional life. Additionally, an advanced German course can be taken voluntarily as part of the "Studium Generale" module.
The programme concludes with the development and defence of a Master's thesis. The thesis is completed under the guidance of faculty experts, allowing students to delve deeply into a specific area of mechanical engineering.

programmes.description:
Our seven-semester Bachelor of Engineering programme, conducted entirely in English, blends engineering sciences with problem-solving, design, and communication skills. It prepares students for a wide range of career options in the field of mechanical engineering and also provides them a solid academic foundation for the continuation of their studies in graduate programmes.
Mechanical Engineering is designed for about 50 to 60 new students per year. Due to the relatively small number of students, a unique trademark of this programme is the students' close personal contact to the staff and faculty members of our department.
As a Mechanical Engineering student, you will learn the fundamentals of engineering design, simulation, and manufacturing, and you will also gain hands-on experience in laboratory settings and through projects with industry partners. Our expert faculty will guide you through coursework in topics such as mechanics, thermodynamics, materials science, numerical methods, computer science, and mechatronics, ensuring that you have a broad understanding of the field and the skills needed to tackle complex engineering challenges.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The first four semesters provide a well-rounded and comprehensive education in the most important fields of mechanical engineering. This foundation enables students to approach problems scientifically to develop practical solutions and also introduces them to the numerous practical fields within mechanical engineering.
The last three semesters comprise advanced coursework and an internship. The degree is completed with an academic paper in the form of a Bachelor’s thesis. Many students choose to collaborate with engineering companies in the region or worldwide for their thesis. The sequence of the last three semesters is flexible, which provides students the opportunity to craft their own learning journey including study abroad semesters.
In addition to imparting specialist knowledge, key skills including learning and working techniques as well as intercultural teamwork and communication are also promoted. For international students eyeing a career in German-speaking countries, German language courses are integrated from the first semester onwards. Meanwhile, native German speakers can enhance their profile with another foreign language.
A special offer for our international students: The first semester will be taught in a hybrid format (teaching in person and online), so students who didn't make it to Germany in time can attend lectures. Students must arrive in Germany before the exam period in January.
programmes.internships:
During the fifth semester, each student completes a 20-week internship. We recommend to do the internship in Germany.
Students have the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals from the industry and to acquire valuable professional skills.
The university gives students information and support in finding and organising an internship.
programmes.partTimeJobs: There will be occasional opportunities to work as an administrative assistant or a tutor (only for advanced students). Part-time jobs outside the university are also available.
programmes.accommodation:
Students can apply for accommodation in student halls of residence, which are close to the university and well equipped. For more information, please follow this link.
Additionally, you can look for a private apartment or a room in a shared flat (which is called a "Wohngemeinschaft" in German, abbreviated as "WG"). Useful information about accommodation can also be found on this website.

programmes.description: From an international perspective, the Bachelor’s degree course of study in Mechanical Engineering is a very typical and traditional engineering degree course for Germany, whose graduates are in high demand on the national and international job market.
programmes.courseOrganisation:
The duration of the Bachelor’s degree programme is 42 months with a total of 210 ECTS that must be earned.
The degree programme is divided into five-week blocks – following our CORE principle. There is an exam for each module in the fifth week. This ensures that competencies are acquired in a focused way.
The Bachelor’s course of study includes a practical phase (internship) and a Bachelor’s thesis (16 weeks).
The programme includes (excerpt):
• Mathematics and natural sciences
• Fundamentals of engineering sciences: from physics and material sciences to engineering mechanics and thermodynamics
• Electrical engineering
• Technical construction and computer aided design
• Product development: innovation und economics
• Automation and control
• Programming
• Introduction to quality management
• Technical thermodynamics
• Automotive and propulsion technology
• Machine elements and dynamics
• Innovation in product development
• Advanced mathematics and numerical analysis: FEM simulation
• Introduction to fluid mechanics
• Heat transfer
• Applied thermo-fluid science
• Elective courses are available: battery technology; professional CAD; medical engineering; power plant engineering; digital transformation–Internet of things (IoT) and many more….
The small student groups (maximum 35 students per group), the mentoring system, and the open-door policy as well as the renowned, experienced teaching staff guarantee special and very individual study conditions and attention.

However, freelance work is not permitted. Internships that are mandatory for the successful completion of your studies at SRH do not count towards the above-named 120 full days.
Employment that is considered “student part-time work” ("studentische Nebentätigkeit", e.g. employment as a student worker at a university or in a university-related organisation or "Werkstudent" activities at companies that are related to your studies) can be done without any time restrictions.

programmes.description:
There is a long-term global demand for graduates with engineering degrees. The central task in almost all industries is the process of inventing and developing new products. This includes product design and product creation. Increasing digitalisation is changing the requirements for new products and production systems. Much more complex "intelligent" products need to be developed and produced in less time. Globalisation is also putting the industry under enormous pressure, which has been exacerbated by the recent crisis. In addition to shorter development times, costs must be significantly reduced in order to remain competitive.
Our Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering combines a broad engineering foundation with application-oriented subjects that teach methods and skills that can be directly applied in professional practice to best meet the needs of industry. In addition, this Bachelor's degree is complemented by a comparatively high level of language and cultural skills, as students come from many different countries. This part of the programme is in line with industry requirements for future graduates. Graduates are increasingly expected to be able to work in a team, speak foreign languages, and have international experience. This programme equips students with these competencies accordingly.

programmes.description:
Study Programme
The new degree programme in Mechanical Engineering (MEB) provides a classical foundation in mechanical engineering and process engineering. The broad and interdisciplinary education enables graduates to work in all areas of the modern economy. In addition to indispensable basics such as mathematics and thermodynamics, subjects such as design and plant planning are taught. The global sustainability aspect is an important pillar of the programme and is considered, for example, in courses such as bioengineering and physical process engineering. Within the Engineering Basics course and during the practical phase, initial contacts with the regional industry will be established, representing the beginning of further employment in the regional economy. The programme concludes with a thesis. After completing the Bachelor's programme in Mechanical Engineering, there is an opportunity (requires further language qualifications) to pursue a Master's degree in the Engineering and Management programme, for example.
Study Goals and Qualification Objectives
Upon completion, graduates will have a solid foundation in essential mechanical engineering and process engineering fundamentals, along with a broad knowledge of practical application and a solid understanding of methods and techniques in the following areas:
• Mechanical basics and component dimensioning for the functional and strength-oriented development and design of component systems
• Manufacturing fundamentals for the economical design of components
• CAX-based systems (CAD, numerics, programming)
• Process and energy engineering fundamentals for the planning and development of process engineering components and systems
• A solid basis of the German language
Employability of Graduates
The classical, comprehensive education in mechanical engineering/process engineering enables graduates to work in all relevant industrial sectors. This includes the development and design of mechanical products and equipment, among others, for process engineering processes. This encompasses production machinery for the automated assembly of pump systems, for example. Additionally, graduates of the new programme will distinguish themselves through important soft skills, which can be acquired in modules such as Engineering Basics and Projects in Mechanical Engineering or Process Engineering.
Possible Fields of Employment
Graduates can find employment with mechanical engineering and process engineering companies in Germany and abroad. The well-known professional profile of a study programme that balances disciplines from mechanical engineering and process engineering opens up opportunities in all typical industry companies, institutions and research facilities at home and all over the world.
